name: Ordos bronzes
date_note: objects 5th c. BCE–9 CE in museum records
making_significance: A museum grouping of steppe-style bronze and gold fittings, buckles and plaques from the Ordos region; most records give no findspot.
leaves_out: the steppe makers and the findspots lost to the market
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1952.115 and search https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/?q=Ordos&cc0=1; Liu et al. 2021 (https://www.nature.com/articles/s40494-021-00520-5); F1.25 spec claims 5, 7, 19. Proposed by F1.12a and F1.25. links: STY098

name: Xianbei
making_significance: A nomadic people whose belt plaques, like the Met's gilded pair, "once adorned a leather belt"; also a polity (F1.25).
notes: Source: Met 24.174.7 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/52109); F1.25 spec claim 9. Proposed as archaeological culture and polity; one row. links: POL161

name: Kongo Christianity
making_significance: Kongo elites shaped a Christianity of their own; Kongo artists varied crucifix figures "far beyond any European precedent".
leaves_out: the Kongo objects the Portuguese demanded destroyed
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/exhibitions/listings/2015/kongo/blog/posts/kongo-christian-art; https://news.yale.edu/2019/03/05/art-historian-cecile-fromont-uncovers-kongos-christian-visual-culture; F1.16 spec claims 8–11. Two readings: imposition or local reinvention. links: GAP054; BEL011

name: Jingpiao
making_significance: Newcomers to Jingdezhen's porcelain workshops; People's Daily counts "60,000 Jingpiaos".
notes: Source: https://en.people.cn/n3/2025/0719/c90000-20342418.html; F1.8 spec claim 22. The source's term; makers' own words via AFP 2023 (F1.8). links: PRA069

name: Rakival People
making_significance: The Rakival People committed in 2020 to work with Melbourne Museum and the PNG Museum on the Lapita finds from their island.
notes: Source: https://collections.museumsvictoria.com.au/api/articles/16774; F1.12 spec claim 13.

name: Bunuba
making_significance: Traditional Owners of Bandiln͟gan (Windjana Gorge), where Carpenter's Gap yielded an early ground-edge hatchet flake.
notes: Source: https://exploreparks.dbca.wa.gov.au/park/bandilngan-windjana-gorge-national-park; https://rockartaustralia.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/Occupation_at_Carpenters_Gap_Oconnor_et_al_2014.pdf; F1.12 spec claim 6. The Bunuba attribution is held for a reader (F1.12 spec §9).

name: Japanese prisoners of war in Uzbekistan
making_significance: Japanese prisoners of war held in Uzbekistan after 1945 "assisted" in the final phase of building the Navoi Theatre.
notes: Source: https://kun.uz/en/20430948; F1.20 spec claim 6. Number and conditions unverified (F1.20 spec §10).

name: Gweagal
making_significance: A clan of Kamay (Botany Bay); spears taken there in 1770 were returned in 2024 to La Perouse representatives "including direct descendants of the Gweagal people".
notes: Source: https://www.trin.cam.ac.uk/news/return-of-the-gweagal-spears-to-the-la-perouse-aboriginal-community/; https://aiatsis.gov.au/whats-new/news/return-gweagal-spears-la-perouse-aboriginal-community; F1.24 spec claim 17. Endonym check open (F1.24 spec §10). links: COM306; PLC482

name: La Perouse Aboriginal Community
making_significance: The Aboriginal community at La Perouse received the four Gweagal spears from Trinity College in 2024.
notes: Source: https://aiatsis.gov.au/whats-new/news/return-gweagal-spears-la-perouse-aboriginal-community; F1.24 spec claim 17.

name: Ngāti Toa Rangatira
making_significance: The iwi whose deed of settlement the Haka Ka Mate Attribution Act 2014 puts into effect.
notes: Source: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2014/0018/latest/whole.html; F1.26 spec claim 11. links: COM288; PRA223

name: Peskotomuhkati
making_significance: The Passamaquoddy (Peskotomuhkati) adapted Traditional Knowledge labels for 1890 cylinder recordings of their songs.
notes: Source: https://www.passamaquoddy.com; https://www.loc.gov/collections/ancestral-voices/about-this-collection/; F1.26 spec claim 16 and §10.

name: Chinos of New Spain
date_note: Manila Galleon era; treated as Indians in law from 1672
making_significance: Enslaved people from South and Southeast Asia brought to Mexico on the Manila Galleon were grouped as chinos; from 1672 the law treated them as Indians.
leaves_out: the many communities the label merged
notes: Source: Seijas, https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/asian-slaves-in-colonial-mexico-from-chinos-to-indians/; F1.13 spec claim 17. A colonial category, not a community's own name. links: NET036

name: Meisterwerke muhammedanischer Kunst (Munich 1910)
making_significance: The Munich exhibition showed more than 3,600 works from about 250 collections in eighty halls, shaping "Islamic art" as a collectors' category.
leaves_out: the makers and the places the works left
notes: Source: Troelenberg 2012, https://arthistoriography.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/05/troelenberg.pdf; F1.3 spec claim 17.

name: "The Persistence of Geometry" (Cleveland, 2006)
making_significance: A Cleveland Museum of Art show at MOCA Cleveland grouped a Mamluk bowl and a Kuba cloth as geometry.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1991.224; F1.15 spec claim 18.

name: "The Venetian Tradition" (Cleveland, 1956–57)
making_significance: A Cleveland show that hung a Mamluk inlaid bowl from Damascus as "Venetian".
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1945.133; F1.15 spec claim 17.

name: Heeramaneck Galleries
making_significance: The New York dealers sold Cleveland the İznik mosque lamp (1944.236) in 1944; the building it hung in is not recorded.
leaves_out: the lamp's earlier owners and the mosque it hung in
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1944.236; F1.1 spec claim 10.

name: Maasai Intellectual Property Initiative
date_note: began 2010, after Maasai leaders approached Light Years IP in 2009
making_significance: A Maasai-led body set out to license the Maasai name and brand, reporting "over 1,000 companies" using it.
notes: Source: https://maasaiintellectualpropertyinitiative.org/faqs; F1.2 spec claim (Concept). links: COM062; PRA030

name: Karamu House and the Gilpin Players
date_note: collected through Paul Travis 1927–28; gifts to Cleveland 1929
making_significance: The Cleveland settlement house's theatre company acquired African carvings through Paul Travis and gave them to the Cleveland Museum of Art.
leaves_out: the carvers and the communities the works left
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1929.342 and 1929.364 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1929.364); F1.2 spec claim 7; F1.6 spec claim on 1929.364. links: PLC423

name: Edison Manufacturing Company
making_significance: Edison's film company made Blacksmith Scene (1893) in the Black Maria with employees acting as smiths; Edison's name stood over Dickson, Heise and the actors.
leaves_out: W. K. L. Dickson, William Heise, Charles Kayser and John Ott
notes: Source: https://www.filmpreservation.org/preserved-films/screening-room/blacksmithing-scene-1893; F1.4 spec claim 1.

name: Victor Talking Machine Company
making_significance: The record company issued descriptive scenes, dance music and the Original Dixieland Jazz Band's 1917 disc.
leaves_out: the session musicians and earlier Black musicians
free_sources: Library of Congress National Jukebox; DAHR (link-out)
notes: Source: https://www.loc.gov/item/jukebox-186254/; https://adp.library.ucsb.edu/index.php/objects/detail/33030/Victor_4106; F1.4 spec claims 5–7.

name: Keur Moussa Abbey
making_significance: Monks at the Senegalese abbey introduced wooden tuning pegs on the kora from 1963.
leaves_out: the griot makers whose instrument it is
notes: Source: https://www.amis.org/post/on-the-organology-of-the-kora; F1.4 spec claim 14.

name: Crosby Brown Collection
making_significance: A collection of world musical instruments given to the Met in 1889; how many left their places of origin is not recorded.
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/501374; https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/501115; F1.4 spec §5.

name: Nagaoka Municipal Science Museum
making_significance: The museum holds the flame pot from Umataka that gave the type its name and published its 3D scan under CC BY.
notes: Source: https://api.sketchfab.com/v3/models/ce7aedf779a741239c664ba3d6c4448a; F1.5 spec claim 10.

name: National Diet Library
making_significance: Japan's national library holds Hyakumantō dharani and calls them "the oldest traceable publication in the world whose production date is clearly identified".
notes: Source: https://www.loc.gov/item/2021667586/; F1.5 spec claim 20.

name: Walters Art Museum
making_significance: The Baltimore museum built on Henry Walters's collection; many records say "date and mode of acquisition unknown".
leaves_out: the routes by which objects reached Walters
notes: Source: Walters records, e.g. https://art.thewalters.org/object/W.591/ and https://art.thewalters.org/object/2011.20.14/; F1.10 spec claim 9; F1.7 spec claim 12.

name: Diné be' Iiná
making_significance: A Diné organisation that runs Sheep Is Life around Navajo-Churro sheep and weaving.

name: Guan da min shao
making_significance: "Moulded by the imperial kiln, fired by the civil kilns": court orders for porcelain were placed with private kilns at Jingdezhen.

name: National Gallery of Australia
making_significance: Australia's national gallery bought the stolen Sripuranthan Nataraja and returned it to India in 2014.

name: Cooper Hewitt
making_significance: The New York design museum publishes open records and public-domain images, among them a 19th-century kain panjang.
free_sources: Cooper Hewitt Open Access (CC0 metadata; images where PD)
notes: Source: https://collection.cooperhewitt.org/objects/18437553/; F1.9 spec §5.

name: Partage
date_note: in Iran after the French monopoly ended in 1930
making_significance: A rule that divided excavated finds between the foreign sponsor and the host country; many museum objects came this way.
leaves_out: local people's claims to the finds
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-metropolitan-museums-excavations-at-qasr-i-abu-nasr; F1.9a spec claim 17. Kind chosen: institution (a legal arrangement); the spec says "practice".

name: IRCICA
other_names: Research Centre for Islamic History, Art and Culture
making_significance: The Istanbul research centre invited Yushaa Abdullah to study calligraphy with Hasan Çelebi from December 2007.
notes: Source: https://www.scriptsnscribes.com/blogs/2021/8/13/a-conversation-with-master-calligrapher-yushaa-abdullah; F1.10 spec claim 23.

name: Amsterdam drapers' guild
making_significance: The guild's sampling officials controlled the quality of wool cloth and commissioned Rembrandt's "The Syndics" for their hall.
leaves_out: Amsterdam's weavers and dyers, whose cloth they judged
notes: Source: Rijksmuseum SK-C-6 (https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/SK-C-6); F1.11 spec claim 16. links: PLC448; POL129

name: Compagnons du Devoir
other_names: Association ouvrière des Compagnons du Devoir et du Tour de France

notes: Source: https://compagnons-du-devoir.com/se-former/devenir-compagnon-du-devoir/; https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/compagnonnage-network-for-on-the-job-transmission-of-knowledge-and-identities-00441; F1.11 spec claims 21–22. links: PRA165

name: Museum Het Valkhof
making_significance: The Nijmegen museum holds the bowl stamped by Utilis of Lyon from the Kops Plateau.
notes: Source: Europeana record as for Utilis; F1.11 spec §5.

name: Badisches Landesmuseum
making_significance: The Karlsruhe museum holds Raab's 1764 masterpiece cabinet, its image released CC0.
notes: Source: https://www.deutsche-digitale-bibliothek.de/item/IMT25HT6PFDQSUBD3VPQNY2L6UDIFISJ; F1.11 spec §5.

name: Elbląska Biblioteka Cyfrowa
making_significance: The Elbląg digital library publishes the 1774 West Prussian craft ordinance as public domain.
notes: Source: https://dlibra.bibliotekaelblaska.pl/dlibra/publication/6298/edition/6072/ordynacya-rzemieslnicza-lub-ulozenie-porzadkow-rzemieslniczych-dla-pruss-zachodnich; F1.11 spec §5.

name: Gundjeihmi Aboriginal Corporation
making_significance: The Mirarr's corporation gave permission for the Madjedbebe research and speaks of "the 65,000-year-old Madjedbebe" site.

name: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation
making_significance: The Gunditjmara Traditional Owners' corporation, the consent route for teaching Budj Bim aquaculture.

name: Polynesian Voyaging Society
making_significance: The Hawaiʻi society sails Hōkūleʻa and teaches wayfinding; F1.12 and F1.28a teach only what PVS and Native Hawaiian sources publish.
notes: Source: https://hokulea.com/history/; F1.12 spec claim 19. links: PRA197; OBT294

name: Museum of Primitive Art
making_significance: The New York museum (its own name, quoted) showed a khipu in its 1963–64 Exhibition of Peruvian Art; its collection and library went to the Met.
leaves_out: the makers and communities, named only by region
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/en/perspectives/goldwater-library; F1.15 spec §4 and §10. The name is the museum's own, quoted; not our word.

name: Society of Jesus
making_significance: The Catholic order ran mission workshops, as in the Guaraní reducciones, until its expulsion from Spanish lands (1767–68).
leaves_out: the Guaraní and other workers in its missions
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/275/; F1.16 spec claim 13. links: MKR027

name: LINE Creators Market
making_significance: The platform sells creators' stickers only after approval against its review guidelines: the platform as commissioner.
notes: Source: https://creator.line.me/en/review_guideline/; F1.17 spec claim 17. links: NET063

name: Didier, Petit et Cie
making_significance: The Lyon firm ordered the woven silk portrait of Jacquard from Michel-Marie Carquillat, after Bonnefond's painting.
notes: Source: Met 31.124 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/222531); F1.17 spec claim 16; F1.19 spec claim 13. Proposed by F1.17 and F1.19. links: PER543; MKR075

name: Abuja Pottery Training Centre
date_note: founded 1952 (1951 is Cardew's appointment); renamed early 1980s or after 1984
making_significance: Michael Cardew's Pottery Training Centre at Abuja trained potters in glazed stoneware; Ladi Kwali joined in December 1954 as its earliest woman trainee.
leaves_out: the Gbari women potters whose methods it drew on
notes: Source: https://post.moma.org/pots-mastery-and-the-enduring-legacy-of-ladi-dosei-kwali/; https://awarewomenartists.com/en/artiste/ladi-kwali/; F1.18 spec claim 17 and §10. links: PER032; PER033

name: Fox, Henderson and Co.
making_significance: The contractors who built the 1851 exhibition hall; Downes published 28 plates from their working drawings in 1852.
notes: Source: https://archive.org/details/McGillLibrary-rbsc_building-erected-hyde-park_folioNA6750L6D71852-21979; F1.19 spec claim 4. links: EVT001

name: Haarlemsche Katoen Maatschappij
making_significance: The Haarlem firm kept making roller-printed imitation batik after 1867; Ebenezer Brown Fleming took its prints to the Gold Coast.
leaves_out: the Gold Coast women traders who chose the designs
notes: Source: https://api.taylorfrancis.com/content/chapters/oa-edit/download?identifierName=doi&identifierValue=10.4324%2F9780429295607-6&type=chapterpdf; F1.19 spec claim 20. links: OBT043; TEC129

name: Naval Camouflage Unit
making_significance: Wilkinson's naval unit, with 11 women art students as assistants, drew dazzle schemes ship by ship.
notes: Source: https://daily.jstor.org/the-camouflage-that-dazzled; https://nmmc.co.uk/2022/04/dazzling-displays/; F1.19a spec claim 11. links: OCC189; PER553

name: Evans Products
making_significance: The firm manufactured the Eameses' moulded plywood leg splints for the US Navy.
notes: Source: https://risdmuseum.org/issue-17-variance/files-eames-leg-splint; F1.19a spec claim 13. links: OBT346

name: Sir J.J. School of Art
other_names: Sir J.J. School of Art, Bombay
making_significance: The Bombay art school hired Lockwood Kipling and John Griffiths from South Kensington in 1865.
notes: Source: https://dagworld.com/the-school-and-the-city-the-j-j-school-of-art-in-bombay.html; F1.19b spec claim 6. Split from INS031. links: INS031

name: Mayo School of Industrial Art (National College of Arts)
making_significance: Opened in Lahore with Kipling as its founding principal "to document the arts and crafts of the Punjab" and train craftsmen.
notes: Source: https://m.nca.edu.pk/introduction.php; F1.19b spec claim 8. Split from INS031. links: INS031; PER554

name: Egyptian School of Fine Arts, Cairo
making_significance: Prince Youssef Kamal paid for a free school with drawing at its core; it trained Mahmoud Mokhtar.
notes: Source: https://www.rem.routledge.com/articles/the-egyptian-school-of-fine-arts; https://finearts.capu.edu.eg/en/about-en/history-of-the-faculty; F1.19b spec claim 18. GAP083 is a different school.

name: "Hand and Eye Work" curriculum (Gold Coast)
making_significance: A colonial school curriculum of handwork and drawing on the Gold Coast, from which the Achimota art department and later the Kumasi art school grew.
notes: Source: https://contemporaryand.com/magazines/past-present-and-future-about-art-in-kumasi/; F1.19b spec claim 19. Interview source. Kind chosen: institution (a curriculum). links: INS003; INS004

name: KNUST architecture department
making_significance: The architecture school at KNUST, Kumasi, where John Owusu-Addo returned to teach.
notes: Source: https://www.vam.ac.uk/articles/about-the-tropical-modernism-exhibition; F1.20 spec claim 14. links: INS004

name: Manufacture Sénégalaise des Arts Décoratifs, Thiès
making_significance: Senegal's national tapestry works; opening it, Senghor called for "un art nouveau pour une nation nouvelle"; four weavers trained in France.

notes: Source: https://mjsc.gouv.sn/manufacture-senegalaise-des-arts-decoratifs-depuis-1966; F1.20 spec claim 16. Thiès as location comes from canon POL240. links: POL240; SCH016

name: Echigoya (Mitsukoshi)
making_significance: Mitsui Takatoshi's Edo drapery sold for cash at fixed prices from 1683; it became the Mitsukoshi department store.
notes: Source: https://www.imhds.co.jp/corporate/business/department/history/history-mitsukoshi.html; F1.21 spec claim 1. links: GAP073

name: Le Bon Marché
date_note: founded 1838 by Paul and Justin Videau; Boucicaut from 1852
making_significance: The Paris store brought in fixed prices, exchanges and refunds under Aristide Boucicaut; staff reached 1,888 by 1879.
defined_by: the European Fashion Heritage Association; LVMH
notes: Source: https://fashionheritage.eu/le-bon-marche; F1.21 spec claim 3. LVMH gives 1852 as the creation date. links: GAP073

name: Abir Congo Company
making_significance: A concession company in the Congo Free State that enforced rubber collection by violence; Harms argues the system failed because the rubber ran out.
notes: Source: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-african-history/article/abs/end-of-red-rubber-a-reassessment1/FD6F01D4842CE513F9F496319FAA2AB9; F1.22 spec claim 6. links: OCC183

name: Creative Growth Art Center
making_significance: An Oakland studio for artists with disabilities, where Judith Scott made her fibre sculptures.
notes: Source: https://www.brooklynmuseum.org/exhibitions/judith_scott; F1.23 spec claim 19.

name: Trinity College, Cambridge
making_significance: The Cambridge college held four Gweagal spears from 1771, agreed their return in March 2023 and handed them over on 23 April 2024.
notes: Source: https://www.trin.cam.ac.uk/news/return-of-the-gweagal-spears-to-the-la-perouse-aboriginal-community/; F1.24 spec claim 17.

name: Allard Pierson Museum
making_significance: The Amsterdam museum's 2014 Crimea exhibition held 565 objects from four Crimean museums; after the annexation Dutch courts sent them to Ukraine.
notes: Source: https://allardpierson.nl/nieuws/alle-objecten-uit-de-krim-terug-in-oekraine/; F1.24 spec claims 8–9. links: OCC333

name: National Museum of the History of Ukraine
making_significance: The Kyiv museum received the Crimean objects from Amsterdam in November 2023.

name: Museum of World Culture, Gothenburg
making_significance: The Gothenburg museum returned Paracas textiles removed by Sven Karell to Peru in three groups (4, 79 and 57).
notes: Source: https://www.elperuano.pe/noticia/124707-peru-recibe-los-ultimos-textiles-de-la-cultura-paracas-que-se-encontraban-en-suecia; F1.24 spec claim 14. Counts differ by source. links: PER503

name: National Commission for Museums and Monuments (Nigeria)
making_significance: Nigeria's heritage body received 29 Benin objects from the Smithsonian on 11 October 2022.

name: Harris Tweed Authority
making_significance: The body certifies Harris Tweed, which must be "Handwoven by the islanders at their homes in the Outer Hebrides", with the Orb mark.

name: LIDCOM
other_names: Sant Rohidas Leather Industries and Charmakar Development Corporation
making_significance: A Maharashtra state corporation that holds the Kolhapuri chappal's GI with LIDKAR; it signed with Prada on 10 December 2025.

name: LIDKAR
other_names: Dr Babu Jagjivanram Leather Industries Development Corporation
making_significance: A state corporation that holds the Kolhapuri chappal's GI with LIDCOM.
notes: Source: https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/story/india%2Fmaharashtra%2Fprada-kolhapuri-chappal-row-two-govt-agencies-officially-hold-gi-tag-for-sandals-3661799; F1.26 spec claim 17.

name: Te Rūnanga o Toa Rangatira
other_names: Te Runanga o Toa Rangatira Incorporated
making_significance: The iwi body that enforces the Ka Mate attribution right by declaratory judgment.
notes: Source: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2014/0018/latest/whole.html; F1.26 spec claim 11 and §10.

name: Saami Council

name: Sámi Parliaments
making_significance: The Sámi Parliaments of Finland, Norway and Sweden, parties to the 2019 Frozen 2 agreement.

name: Ájtte, Swedish Mountain and Sámi Museum
making_significance: The Jokkmokk museum received 541 Sámi objects from Sweden's National Museums of World Culture in 2023 and 2025.

name: South African San Council
making_significance: The council of the Khomani, !Xun and Khwe launched a research code requiring council approval, real consent, benefit sharing and results returned.

name: Sealaska Corporation
making_significance: The Tlingit, Haida and Tsimshian corporation gave two Sitka spruce logs for the canoe Hawaiʻiloa when Hawaiʻi's koa forests could not supply one.
notes: Source: https://archive.hokulea.com/ike/kalai_waa/hawaiiloa.html; F1.28a spec claim 15. links: COM092; INS117

name: Te Kohinga Harakeke o Aotearoa
making_significance: The national harakeke collection of 50 varieties, donated by Rene Orchiston, used by weavers for leaf pliability, colour and fibre.
notes: Source: https://www.landcareresearch.co.nz/resources/collections/harakeke/rene-orchiston-collection-catalogue; F1.29 spec claim 15. Cultivar names linked, not quoted (AR-041). links: TEC132

name: Oral History Association
making_significance: The association's ethics call the narrator "the original recording's copyright holder" and give review, restriction and deletion rights.
notes: Source: https://oralhistory.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/2025-OHA-PrinciplesBP_Statement-on-Ethics.pdf; https://oralhistory.org/best-practices/; F1.29 spec claims 2–3.

name: Archives of American Art Oral History Program
making_significance: The Archives of American Art records craft makers' oral histories; narrators review and correct transcripts.
notes: Source: https://www.aaa.si.edu/collections/interviews/oral-history-interview-billie-ruth-sudduth-13623; F1.29 spec claim 19.

name: Repartimiento de comercio
making_significance: Officials advanced goods and credit to Indigenous producers in Oaxaca for cochineal and cloth: forced production in one reading, voluntary but costly credit in Baskes's.
notes: Source: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-latin-american-studies/article/abs/coerced-or-voluntary-the-repartimiento-and-market-participation-of-peasants-in-late-colonial-oaxaca/5111EDBF242AA2B08938DE028E4FD27F; F1.30a spec claim 13. Two readings; held for a reader (F1.30a spec §9).

name: A:shiwi A:wan Museum and Heritage Center
making_significance: The Zuni community museum commissioned map paintings by Zuni artists from 2006.
notes: Source: http://www.ashiwi-museum.org/exhibitions/; F1.31 spec claim 14. Link-out only. links: COM099

name: Barley
date_note: as counted on Uruk tablets, c. 3100–2900 BCE
making_significance: Barley was grown, rationed and counted; on proto-cuneiform tablets it served as crop, ration and unit of account.
leaves_out: the farmers and ration receivers, who are not named
notes: Source: Met 1988.433.1 and 1988.433.2 "barley and emmer" (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/327384); F1.1 spec claims 1–4. The Met says the tablet "most likely" records grain distributed by a large temple.

name: Beech
making_significance: Thonet's chairs were bent from beech; the Koryčany factory stood in Moravian beech forests.
leaves_out: the forest workers who felled it
notes: Source: AIC 1999.556 (https://api.artic.edu/api/v1/artworks/154051); Koryčany town library (https://www.korycany.knihovna.cz/osobnosti/michael-thonet/); F1.1 spec claims 15, 17. links: TEC137; INS062

name: Churro sheep wool
making_significance: Spanish colonists brought churro sheep in 1598; Diné weavers spun their wool, and Sheep Is Life keeps the breed today.
notes: Source: https://joebenwheat.org/resources/glossary-of-southwest-weaving/; https://dinelanduse.org/hweeldi/; F1.7 spec claim 22; F1.25 spec claim 11.

name: Bayeta
making_significance: Trade cloth, often red, that Diné weavers unravelled and rewove as weft.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: https://joebenwheat.org/resources/glossary-of-southwest-weaving/; Cleveland 1921.556 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1921.556); F1.25 spec claims 10–12.

name: Germantown yarn
making_significance: Commercial American yarn dyed with aniline, originally made in Germantown, Pennsylvania, used by Diné weavers in eye-dazzler blankets.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: https://joebenwheat.org/resources/glossary-of-southwest-weaving/; Cleveland 1929.922; F1.25 spec claims 11, 14. Cleveland 1929.922's title says Germantown; its technique field does not.

name: Rag paper
making_significance: Paper made from reused cloth rags; F1.10 reads it as reuse, and the rag collectors are among those its records leave out.
free_sources: link-out (Bloom, Silk Road journal, open access)
notes: Source: Bloom, https://edspace.american.edu/silkroadjournal/wp-content/uploads/sites/984/2017/09/Silk-Road-or-Paper-Road.pdf; F1.10 spec claims 6–8 and §6. links: MAT105; TEC185

name: Böttger stoneware
making_significance: A hard red stoneware made at Meissen in Böttger's period, before and beside its porcelain.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1947.285 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1947.285); F1.14 spec §5. links: PER402

name: Fustian
date_note: allowed for printing by the 1736 Act
making_significance: Cloth with a linen warp and cotton weft; the 1736 Act let British printers work it while printed calicoes were banned.
free_sources: Wikisource (public domain text); Met Open Access
notes: Source: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Ruffhead_-_The_Statutes_at_Large_-_vol_6.djvu/268; Met 1970.237.3; F1.14 spec claims 14–15. links: OCC092; MKR097

name: Rare-earth elements
making_significance: China mined 270,000 of about 380,000 tonnes of rare earths in 2024; processing leaves acid, wastewater and radioactive residue.
notes: Source: https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-rare-earths.pdf; F1.22 spec claim 18.

name: Kermes
making_significance: An insect red used in Europe and West Asia before cochineal replaced it.
notes: Source: Phipps 2010 (https://ia800509.us.archive.org/19/items/CochinealRedthearthistoryofacolor/CochinealRedthearthistoryofacolor_djvu.txt); F1.30a spec claim 10. links: MAT043; MAT042

name: Original Dixieland Jazz Band
making_significance: A white New Orleans band's 1917 Victor disc is often cited as the earliest jazz record issued; earlier Black musicians had recorded.
leaves_out: the Black musicians who made the music before them
notes: Source: https://www.loc.gov/item/jukebox-186254/; F1.4 spec claims 6–7. Contested claim: Reading A earliest known commercially issued jazz record; Reading B a white band recording a Black music.

name: Mainz joiners' guild
making_significance: The joiners' guild of Mainz admitted masters on a masterpiece, its drawing and a written description.
leaves_out: journeymen and apprentices who never became masters
notes: Source: https://www.deutsche-digitale-bibliothek.de/item/IMT25HT6PFDQSUBD3VPQNY2L6UDIFISJ; F1.11 spec claim 17. links: PER514

name: Ri-metos
making_significance: Marshallese navigators who memorised stick charts (mattang, meddo) that were "not even brought along on journeys".
notes: Source: https://ocean.si.edu/human-connections/history-cultures/navigating-waters-micronesian-stick-charts; F1.12 spec claim 16. links: OBT141; TEC214

name: Bromley Hall Printworks
making_significance: The London printworks copperplate-printed fustians whose foliage "recalls" Indian palampores.
notes: Source: Met 1970.237.3 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/229298); F1.14 spec claim 15. links: MAT136

name: De Grieksche A
making_significance: Adrianus Kocx's Delft factory, whose "AK" mark Chinese potters copied on porcelain about 1700.
notes: Source: https://www.aronson.com/east-meets-west/ (dealer); F1.14 spec claim 11. Probable only.

name: Decorative Arts Society, Chicago
making_significance: The Chicago society embroidered May Morris's Lotus door curtain in 1888 for Frances Glessner's parlour.
notes: Source: AIC 1918.298 (https://www.artic.edu/artworks/74514); F1.18 spec claim 11. links: MKR076

name: Chance Brothers, Smethwick
making_significance: The Smethwick glassworks supplied 293,655 panes for the 1851 hall, blown as cylinders and flattened, recruiting French glassworkers for the order.
notes: Source: https://www.vam.ac.uk/articles/the-great-exhibition-of-1851; http://tomchance.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/Glazing_the_Crystal_Palace.pdf; F1.19 spec claims 2–3. links: EVT001

name: Oner Art Combine
making_significance: The Almaty art combine whose brigades made dozens of monumental works, such as the mosaic Qyz Zhibek (1971) by Nikolai Tsivchinsky and Moldakhmet Kenbaev.
notes: Source: https://www.new-east-archive.org/features/show/11093/almaty-monumental-art-dennis-keen; F1.20 spec claim 12. Single interview source.

name: Ngonge clan
making_significance: Craftsmen of the Ngonge clan, headed by a hereditary kaboggoza, made barkcloth for the Buganda royal family.
notes: Source: https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/barkcloth-making-in-uganda-00139; F1.27 spec claim 16. links: OBT047; TEC108

name: Nahua authors of the Florentine Codex
making_significance: The Getty names seven Nahua authors and artists of the Florentine Codex: Antonio Valeriano, Alonso Vegerano, Martín Jacobita, Pedro de San Buenaventura, Diego de Grado, Bonifacio Maximiliano, Mateo Severino.
notes: Source: https://florentinecodex.getty.edu/book/10/folio/123r; https://www.loc.gov/item/2021667837/; F1.28 spec claims 14, 16. The LoC record lists one creator, Sahagún. links: PER076; MKR020

name: Khambhat bead makers
making_significance: Khambhat craftspeople took part in experiments by Kenoyer and Vidale on drilling Indus beads, "at least two to ten hours" per centimetre of agate.
notes: Source: https://asc.iitgn.ac.in/assets/research/completed_projects/Overview_of_Stone_Bead_Drilling_Technology_from_earliest_to_Harappan_times_VN_Prabhakar_2016.pdf; F1.28a spec claim 18. links: MAT006

name: Leidsche Katoenmaatschappij
making_significance: The Leiden cotton firm made imitation batik for Asia, Africa and Suriname; it "never really caught on" in Indonesia but found a market in West Africa.
notes: Source: https://textielmuseum.nl/en/news/Hidden-stories-LKM; F1.30a spec claim 14. links: OBT043; TEC129

name: Design fiction
making_significance: Julian Bleecker defined design fiction as "making things that tell stories".
leaves_out: design traditions outside the Euro-American studio
notes: Source: https://nearfuturelaboratory.com/blog/2009/03/design-fiction-a-short-essay-on-design-science-fact-and-fiction/; F1.30a spec claim 17. links: MOV031; MOV032

name: British gun trade on the West African coast (to 1807)
making_significance: British guns were traded on the West African coast; Satia argues state demand shaped British gun-making, with output rising to millions by 1815.
leaves_out: the people the trade bought and sold
notes: Source: https://southasia.stanford.edu/news/how-british-gun-manufacturers-changed-industrial-world-lock-stock-and-barrel-lorraine; F1.19a spec claim 17. People and goods are never drawn as one flow (F1.19a spec). links: NET035

name: Chinese contract labour in Peru (1849–1874)
making_significance: Nearly 100,000 Chinese men, many "kidnapped or lured", were brought to Peru to work guano fields, railways and plantations 14 to 16 hours a day.
notes: Source: https://www.encyclopedia.com/humanities/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/chinese-labor-peru; F1.22 spec claim 8. People drawn as people, never as goods (F1.22 spec). links: NET061; PLC474

name: Salaula
making_significance: Second-hand clothing in Zambia, Bemba for "selecting from a pile by rummaging"; tailors refit clothes "to fit their new wearers".
notes: Source: https://www.kci.or.jp/articles/files/K_D64_HANSEN_The_Secondhand_Clothing_ENG.pdf; F1.22a spec claim 17.

name: Chinese export porcelain
making_significance: Chinese porcelain factories decorated wares for European buyers, at times copying European prints, as on a dish after a La Fontaine fable.
leaves_out: the painters who copied prints they did not choose
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1970.48 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/?accession_number=1970.48); F1.2 spec claim 1. NET054 covers only the trade (F1.2 spec). links: NET054; STY029

name: Noh mask
making_significance: Carvers make new masks by referring to honmen, old masks held by performing families, so a face is made from a model.
leaves_out: the carver of the Cleveland mask, not recorded
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1972.69 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1972.69); F1.4 spec §1 and §5.

name: Hyakumantō darani
making_significance: Empress Shōtoku ordered a million small wooden pagodas, each holding a printed dharani, after her court suppressed a rebellion in 764.
notes: Source: Met 30.47a–c (https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/44955); F1.5 spec claim 20; F1.16 spec. links: PER532; OCC306

name: Qompi (cumbi cloth)
making_significance: Fine tapestry cloth, "distributed by the Inca ruler" to mark rank.
notes: Source: Walters 2011.20.14 (https://art.thewalters.org/object/2011.20.14/); F1.7 spec claim 12. Merged: F1.7 proposed cumbi as a technique, F1.18 as an object type. links: MKR023

name: Llauto
making_significance: A woven head band from Paracas burials; Cleveland's turban band is one.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1946.228 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1946.228); F1.7 spec §5. links: ARC205

name: Diné wearing blanket
making_significance: Diné women wove blankets to wear around the shoulders; later "wearing blankets … were purchased as rugs" by outside buyers.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1921.556 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1921.556); F1.22a spec claim 10; F1.7 spec §5. links: STY078; PRA035

name: Chief blanket
making_significance: Rugs were modelled on the "chief blanket", though the Diné had no chiefs; after Bosque Redondo weavers turned to goods for outside collectors.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1937.903 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1937.903); F1.22a spec claim 11. links: OBT331

name: Diné rug
making_significance: Diné weavers made floor rugs for trading posts and outside buyers in place of garments.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1937.903 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1937.903); F1.7 spec §5. links: STY078; PRA035

name: Celadon roof tile
making_significance: Goryeo potters made celadon tiles for a royal pavilion roof.
notes: Source: NMK 증2346 (https://www.museum.go.kr/ENG/contents/E0403000000.do?schM=relic_represent_view&relicId=3129); F1.8 spec §5. links: PLC440; PLC198

name: Kain panjang
making_significance: A long wrapped cloth patterned in batik; Cooper Hewitt's example is cotton, "wax resist dyeing (batik) on plain weave".
leaves_out: the town and maker, not recorded
notes: Source: Cooper Hewitt 1961-115-27 (https://collection.cooperhewitt.org/objects/18437553/); F1.9 spec claim 25. links: PRA120; TEC121

name: Inscribed palm stalk
making_significance: Palm stalks holding letters, accounts, contracts and quittances signed by witnesses.
notes: Source: https://anetoday.org/stein-arabia-documents/; https://archaeopresspublishing.com/ojs/index.php/PSAS/article/view/254; F1.9a spec claim 23.

name: Canoe splashboard
making_significance: Trobriand canoes carried carved splashboards on voyages to exchange ceremonial objects (kula).
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1966.130 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1966.130); F1.12 spec claim 14. Link-out only (AR-071). links: NET047

name: Khokhuur
making_significance: A leather vessel in which Mongolian herders make airag.
notes: Source: https://ich.unesco.org/en/state/mongolia-MN?info=elements-on-the-lists; F1.12a spec claim 23. links: PRA087

name: Koshma
making_significance: A felt mat; the Turkestan Album shows Kyrgyz makers preparing koshma ("Prigotovlenie koshm").
notes: Source: LC-DIG-ppmsca-15092 (https://www.loc.gov/item/2007681438/); F1.12a spec §10. links: TEC100

name: Kraak porcelain
making_significance: Chinese export porcelain in underglaze blue, named after the Portuguese carracks the Dutch captured.
notes: Source: Rijksmuseum AK-RBK-16385 (https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/200107018); F1.13 spec claim 18. links: OCC072; NET054

name: Delftware
making_significance: Tin-glazed earthenware from Delft that began by copying Chinese porcelain; Chinese potters in turn copied a Delft factory's mark.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: https://www.aronson.com/east-meets-west/ (dealer); F1.14 spec claim 11 and §1. Kind chosen: object type (the spec offers style or object type). links: MKR071; PLC354; TEC032

name: Pilgrim badge
making_significance: Cast tin-lead badges sold to pilgrims at shrines such as Canterbury, made for use and sale.
notes: Source: Met 2001.310 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/473470); F1.16 spec claim 20. links: PLC458

name: Nanban lectern (shokendai)
making_significance: Catholic missionaries in Japan commissioned lacquer church furnishings, including a folding lectern with the IHS emblem.
notes: Source: https://www.kyohaku.go.jp/old/eng/theme/floor1_6/past/laq_20141126.html; F1.16 spec claim 16. No open record found. links: GAP005

name: Company-monogram porcelain
making_significance: Chinese potters painted Dutch company orders with the VOC monogram and the Republic's arms.
notes: Source: Rijksmuseum AK-NM-2611 (https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/20025519); F1.17 spec claim 12. links: POL238; NET054

name: Digital sticker
making_significance: A small image sold on a messaging platform after review; LINE rejects stickers "not easy to use in daily conversation".
notes: Source: https://creator.line.me/en/review_guideline/; F1.17 spec claim 17. links: INS120

name: Wallpaper
making_significance: Printed paper hangings; May Morris's Honeysuckle (1883) was credited to her father in 1890 and to her in a catalogue of about 1909.
leaves_out: the women designers credited to others
notes: Source: https://wmgallery.org.uk/object/honeysuckle-wallpaper/; F1.18 spec claim 10. links: MKR076

name: Nasij (cloth of gold)
making_significance: Silk woven with gold, which the Mongols had made by weaving communities they moved from Central Asia and Persia to China.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0); Met Open Access
notes: Source: Cleveland 1989.50 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1989.50); Met 64101; F1.19a spec claims 5, 8; F1.28 spec claim 20. Merged: "cloth of gold" proposed by F1.28 too. links: OCC035

name: Moulded plywood leg splint
date_note: Second World War; initial order 5,000; over 150,000 by the war's end
making_significance: Charles and Ray Eames's moulded plywood splint for the US Navy; Evans Products made more than 150,000.
notes: Source: https://risdmuseum.org/issue-17-variance/files-eames-leg-splint; F1.19a spec claim 13. Proposed as an object; filed as an object type (mass-produced). links: PER152; PER153; INS126

name: CC41 mark
making_significance: Each piece of Utility furniture was priced in units and stamped CC41.
notes: Source: https://museum.wales/blog/2168/Rationing-furniture-during-the-Second-World-War-/; F1.19a spec claim 14. links: OCC217

name: Hmong story cloth
making_significance: Hmong story cloths developed in refugee camps, made by men as well as women; some say a relief worker suggested picture embroidery.
notes: Source: https://www.hmongstudiesjournal.org/uploads/4/5/8/7/4587788/craighsj11.pdf; F1.19a spec claim 19. The other name paj ntaub is standard usage, not in the spec.

name: Funpon
making_significance: Kano model books reproduced paintings "faithfully or in rough sketches in smaller size" and were "zealously guarded".
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-kano-school-of-painting; F1.19b spec claim 2. links: SCH040; PER556

name: Siyah mashq
making_significance: Practice pages "intended to strengthen a calligrapher's hand" through repeated letters; after the 16th century they became an art form.
notes: Source: Met 2016.536 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/716307); F1.19b spec claim 4.

name: Mosaic panel
making_significance: Soviet-era monumental mosaics on public buildings; Uzbekistan listed about 157 panels as monumental art in 2024, though one was dismantled in 2023.
notes: Source: https://www.gazeta.uz/en/2024/03/26/mosaic/; F1.20 spec claims 11–12. links: TEC162

name: Ōtsu-e
making_significance: Folk pictures sold at Ōtsu; Yanagi Sōetsu remounted one, with knobs by Hamada Shōji, drawing it into Mingei.
notes: Source: Met 1975.268.147 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/36115); F1.20 spec §5. links: MOV096

name: Pierre Jeanneret's Chandigarh furniture
making_significance: Office and library chairs made for Chandigarh's buildings, credited by the Met to Pierre Jeanneret and by V&A captions in part to Eulie Chowdhury; many were later sold at auction.
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/629168; https://theconversation.com/tropical-modernism-architecture-and-independence-at-vanda-reintroduces-indian-and-ghanaian-pioneers-of-the-style-224556; F1.20 spec claim 15. Maker credit contested. links: PER255

name: Ensi
making_significance: A Turkmen pile hanging that "likely served … to cover the entrance" to a tent made to be "collapsible and portable".
notes: Source: Met 22.100.42 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/447501); F1.22a spec claim 8. links: COM210

name: Chuval
making_significance: Turkmen storage bags held family belongings, "akin to a wardrobe".
notes: Source: Met 22.100.40a (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/447498); F1.22a spec claim 8. links: COM210

name: Darning sampler
making_significance: Samplers on which girls learned "to mend worn places and holes", made in five north European countries.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: https://www.trc-leiden.nl/trc-needles/individual-textiles-and-textile-types/samplers/darning-sampler; https://clevelandart.org/art/1942.528; F1.22a spec claim 16. links: TEC224

name: Jaipur foot
making_significance: A rubber prosthetic foot that needed no shoe, suiting people who "go barefoot", by P. K. Sethi and the craftsman Ram Chandra Sharma.
notes: Source: https://blog.sciencemuseum.org.uk/jaipur-foot-the-low-cost-prosthetic-that-revolutionised-medical-care-in-india-and-beyond/; F1.22a spec claim 19. links: PER580; PER581

name: Convict love token
making_significance: Tokens made by convicts; about 350 are known, "one of the few classes of items convicts made … purely of their own volition".
notes: Source: https://collection.powerhouse.com.au/object/12096; F1.23 spec claim 16.

name: Storage jar
making_significance: Large jars for storing food and drink; Dave's 25-gallon jar of 1858 carries his signature and a couplet.
notes: Source: Met 2020.7 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/747045); F1.23 spec claim 1.

name: Belt plaque
making_significance: Cast metal plaques worn on belts across the steppe and in China, from the Xigoupan gold plaques to the Xianbei pair.
notes: Source: Met 24.174.7 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/52109); https://www.nature.com/articles/s40494-021-00520-5; F1.25 spec claims 7, 9. links: ARC231; STY098

name: "Tre lune" watermark
date_note: in Egyptian documents as early as 1631
making_significance: Venetian papermakers marked paper for Ottoman markets with three crescents; Saharan copyists wrote on it.
notes: Source: https://blogs.lib.umich.edu/beyond-reading-room/watermark-wednesdays-three-crescents; F1.27 spec claim 10.

name: Scribe's palette
making_significance: The Egyptian scribe's working tool; Cleveland's wooden example dates 1540–1186 BCE.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1914.727 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1914.727); F1.28 spec §5. links: OBT065

name: Felt carpet
making_significance: Kyrgyz felt carpets of two types, with "the semantics of ornamentation" part of the element; women are "the principal bearers".
notes: Source: https://ich.unesco.org/en/USL/ala-kiyiz-and-shyrdak-art-of-kyrgyz-traditional-felt-carpets-00693; F1.29 spec claim 7. links: PRA160

name: Fanner basket
making_significance: Coiled baskets used to separate rice from husks, made by Gullah Geechee makers and in Senegal.
leaves_out: enslaved rice workers; historians' terms quoted
notes: Source: https://americanart.si.edu/artwork/gullah-fanner-basket-82599; https://nmaahc.si.edu/object/nmaahc_2014.96.2; F1.29 spec claims 11–12. links: COM115; PER602

name: Navajo Nation v. Urban Outfitters (2012–2016)
other_names: Navajo Nation v. Urban Outfitters, Inc. (D.N.M. 1:12-cv-00195)
making_significance: The Navajo Nation sued a retailer over "Navajo" products under its trademarks and settled with a licence and supply agreement.
defined_by: the court record; the Navajo Nation
leaves_out: Diné weavers whose designs were not themselves protected
notes: Source: https://narf.org/nill/bulletins/federal/documents/navajo_nation_v_urban_outfitters_2016.html; https://indianz.com/News/2016/11/17/navajo-nation-settles-dispute-over-sale.asp; F1.2 spec claim 11; F1.24 spec claim 20. links: COM097; PRA035

name: Tlahuitoltepec blouse case (2015)
making_significance: The Ayuujk community of Santa María Tlahuitoltepec said a Paris designer's 2015 collection copied its blouse; a separate Paris suit found Antik Batik held no rights.
defined_by: the community's authorities; the Paris court
leaves_out: the women who embroider the blouse
notes: Source: https://www.viveoaxaca.org/2015/06/PronunciamientoTlahuitoltepecPlagio2015.html; https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/isabel-marant-freed-of-plagiarism-accusations/2015120818656; F1.2 spec claims 17–18. links: COM124; OBT040

name: In re Southern Rhodesia (1919)
making_significance: The Privy Council denied African land rights on the ground that "some tribes are so low in the scale of social organization"; Mabo (1992) rejected that basis.
leaves_out: the Africans whose land was decided
notes: Source: https://henley.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/journals/AULegHist/2007/13.html; F1.3 spec claim 3.

name: Mabo v Queensland (No 2) (1992)
making_significance: The High Court of Australia quoted the 1919 Privy Council and called that theory "false in fact", recognising native title.
notes: Source: http://www.mabonativetitle.com/info/recognitionNT.htm; https://henley.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/journals/AULegHist/2007/13.html; F1.3 spec claim 3.

name: Rhodesian censorship of Great Zimbabwe archaeology (1970s)
making_significance: In 1970 the Rhodesian Front government told its employees that no official publication might say plainly that Great Zimbabwe was an African creation.
leaves_out: the Shona descendants of the builders
notes: Source: https://sas-space.sas.ac.uk/4213/1/Preben_Kaarsholm_-_The_past_as_battlefield_in_Rhodesia_and_Zimbabwe.pdf; F1.3 spec claim 15. links: PLC087; POL015

name: Navajo delegation to Washington (1874)
making_significance: A Diné delegation travelled to Washington in 1874; a loom with unfinished weavings came with it into the national collection.
notes: Source: https://www.si.edu/object/nmnhanthropology_8345504; F1.7 spec claim 24. links: PER501; COM097

name: Naaltsoos Sání (1868)
making_significance: The Diné-named treaty of 1868 ended the imprisonment at Hwéeldi and returned the people to Diné Bikéyah, where weaving resumed for new markets.
defined_by: Diné authors (Raymond D. Austin); the Navajo Times
notes: Source: https://dinelanduse.org/hweeldi/; https://navajotimes.com/reznews/hweeldi-150/; F1.7 spec claim 22. links: OCC141; COM097

name: Peru Law 6634 (1929)
making_significance: Peru barred the export of archaeological objects without government permission; no permit is recorded for many later exports.
notes: Source: https://arqueologia.deperu.com/6634.php; F1.7 spec claim 6.

name: Sheep Is Life
making_significance: An annual Diné gathering around churro sheep and weaving where weavers speak for themselves.
notes: Source: https://navajotimes.com/entertainment/2011/0611/063011sheep2.php; F1.7 spec claim 25. links: INS104; MAT131

name: Korea's 1916 Regulations
other_names: Regulations for the Preservation of Ancient Sites and Relics (1916)
making_significance: Colonial Korea required finds to be reported, items registered and digs permitted; registered items needed inspection before export.
leaves_out: Koreans who had no say in the rules
notes: Source: https://www.eastasian.ucsb.edu/wp-content/uploads/CreationNationalTreasures2001.pdf; F1.8 spec claim 11.

name: China's 1930 Law on the Preservation of Antiquities
date_note: law of 2 June 1930; export rules from 1935
making_significance: China's antiquities law dates from 2 June 1930, with export rules from 1935.
notes: Source: Zhang 2022, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s43238-022-00057-x; F1.8 spec §5.

name: Emi rebellion (764)
making_significance: After the court suppressed this rebellion, Empress Shōtoku commissioned the One Million Pagodas in thanks.
notes: Source: Met 30.47a–c (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/44955); F1.16 spec claim 4. links: OBT326; PER532

name: Sripuranthan Nataraja theft and return (2006–2014)
making_significance: A Chola Nataraja stolen from Sripuranthan was sold to the National Gallery of Australia in 2008 and handed back to India in 2014.
notes: Source: https://nga.gov.au/media/dd/documents/qa_update_shiva_nataraja.pdf; https://indiankanoon.org/doc/14478654; F1.9 spec claims 13–14. The 2006 start rests on an encyclopaedia (probable).

name: Antiquities and Art Treasures Act (1972)
making_significance: India's law covers objects at least 100 years old; only the central government or its agency may export them.
notes: Source: https://asi.nic.in/pdf/antiquityAct.pdf; F1.9 spec claim 16.

name: Rubin v. Islamic Republic of Iran (2018)
making_significance: The US Supreme Court held that the Persepolis Fortification tablets on loan in Chicago could not be seized to pay a judgment against Iran.
notes: Source: https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/583/16-534; F1.9a spec §10. Wording held for a Historian reader (F1.9a spec).

name: Met Persian Expedition (1932–35)
making_significance: The Met's excavations in Iran, at Qasr-i Abu Nasr among others, sent finds to New York through partage.
leaves_out: the Iranian workers on the digs
notes: Source: Yates 2018, https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-metropolitan-museums-excavations-at-qasr-i-abu-nasr; F1.9a spec claim 17.

name: West Prussian craft ordinance (1774)
making_significance: A craft ordinance for West Prussia, in 49 paragraphs, bound craftsmen to standards "under threat of penalty".
notes: Source: https://dlibra.bibliotekaelblaska.pl/dlibra/publication/6298/edition/6072/ordynacya-rzemieslnicza-lub-ulozenie-porzadkow-rzemieslniczych-dla-pruss-zachodnich; F1.11 spec claim 18. links: INS114

name: Lake Condah drainage (1954)
making_significance: Lake Condah (Tae Rak), part of the Budj Bim system, "was drained in 1954"; the community has worked to restore it with a weir.
notes: Source: https://latrobejournal.slv.vic.gov.au/latrobejournal/issue/latrobe-85/t1-g-t8.html; F1.12 spec claim 8. Restoration dates not reached. links: PLC391; PRA211

name: First Nations cultural protocols, third edition (2020)
other_names: Protocols for using First Nations Cultural and Intellectual Property in the Arts (3rd ed.)
making_significance: Creative Australia's protocols (Terri Janke) set ten principles for First Nations cultural and intellectual property; funded projects must comply.
defined_by: Australia Council (now Creative Australia); Terri Janke
notes: Source: https://creative.gov.au/first-nations-arts/protocols-for-using-first-nations-cultural-and-intellectual-property-in-the-arts; https://apo.org.au/node/308574; F1.12 spec claim 21; F1.31 spec claim 13.

name: Han acquisition of Central Asian horses (1st century BCE)
making_significance: Chinese envoys brought Bactrian horses to the Han capital; the court called them "heavenly horses" and linked them with dragons.
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/perspectives/lunar-new-year-2; F1.12a spec claim 17. A Han source is still to read (F1.12a spec §9).

name: Dürer's imperial privilege (1511)
making_significance: Dürer's book edition of the Life of the Virgin warned "thieves and imitators" that the images carried Maximilian I's imperial privilege.
notes: Source: https://artmuseum.princeton.edu/art/collections/objects/18191; F1.14 spec claim 3. links: PER392

name: SCAPIN-1535, "Made in Occupied Japan" (1947)
making_significance: The occupation authority ordered every Japanese export article, container and package marked "Made in Occupied Japan".
notes: Source: https://jahis.law.nagoya-u.ac.jp/scapindb/docs/scapin-1535; F1.14 spec claim 18.

name: Getty Images v Stability AI (2025)
making_significance: A UK court found an AI model was not an "infringing copy" of the images it was trained on; permission to appeal that point was granted in December 2025.
leaves_out: the photographers whose images were used
notes: Source: https://www.judiciary.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Getty-Images-v-Stability-AI.pdf; F1.14 spec claim 20. Also proposed by F1.21. links: GAP029

name: US Copyright Office report on generative AI training (2025)
making_significance: The Office wrote that commercial use of "vast troves" of works to make competing content goes beyond fair use, "especially where … illegal access".
notes: Source: https://copyright.gov/ai/Copyright-and-Artificial-Intelligence-Part-3-Generative-AI-Training-Report-Pre-Publication-Version.pdf; F1.14 spec claim 20. Also proposed by F1.21. links: GAP029

name: Canut revolt (1831)
making_significance: Several hundred Lyon silk weavers rose at the Croix-Rousse when manufacturers refused the agreed piece rates; about 600 died.
notes: Source: https://www.gadagne-lyon.fr/sites/gadagne/files/medias/documents/2020-11/MHL-Gadagne_FicheTheme_19e-InsurrectionsDesCanuts.pdf; F1.19 spec claim 14. links: MKR075

name: Canut revolt (1834)
making_significance: The Lyon silk weavers rose again; more than 600 died.
notes: Source: https://www.gadagne-lyon.fr/sites/gadagne/files/medias/documents/2020-11/MHL-Gadagne_FicheTheme_19e-InsurrectionsDesCanuts.pdf; F1.19 spec claim 14. links: MKR075; OCC319

name: Housing (Temporary Accommodation) Act (1944)
making_significance: The Act allowed up to £150 million; 156,623 prefab bungalows were built 1945–49, meant to last no more than a decade.
notes: Source: https://heritagecalling.com/2022/08/04/a-brief-history-of-prefabs/; F1.19a spec claim 15. links: OBT028

name: Ministry of Information posters (1939)
making_significance: The Ministry of Information had three posters; "Keep calm and carry on" was printed and held in reserve for a severe air raid.
notes: Source: https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/education/resources/home-front-1939-1945-part-two/ministry-of-information-posters/; F1.19a spec claim 16. links: OBT135

name: Tashkent earthquake (1966)
making_significance: The earthquake led to Tashkent's rebuilding with Soviet modernist buildings, ten of which UNESCO inscribed in 2026.
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1766/; F1.20 spec claim 9.

name: Mitsukoshi Department Store Declaration (1904)
making_significance: On its incorporation Mitsukoshi Gofukuten issued a "Department Store Declaration", after display selling (1895) and the end of seated selling (1900).
notes: Source: https://www.imhds.co.jp/corporate/business/department/history/history-mitsukoshi.html; F1.21 spec claim 2. links: INS133

name: "Haute Couture" designation (1945)
making_significance: "Haute Couture" became a legally registered designation in France.
notes: Source: https://www.fhcm.paris/en/our-history; F1.21 spec claim 7. links: GAP072

name: Simplified Arabic (1954)
making_significance: A Linotype Arabic for Al-Hayat that cut the character count so Arabic fitted one 90-channel magazine; Compugraphic later copied it.
leaves_out: the calligraphers whose forms were cut
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Arabic; F1.21 spec claim 13. links: PER575; STY114

name: Project 748 (1974)
making_significance: China's project to typeset Chinese electronically; a book printed in 1980 marked the move from "lead and fire" to "light and electricity".
notes: Source: https://newsen.pku.edu.cn/news_events/news/people/8889.html; F1.21 spec claim 14. links: PER576; PER577

name: Linotype Bengali (1978–82)
making_significance: Fiona Ross and Tim Holloway designed Linotype Bengali for newspaper composition; Ross says early fonts were "hampered by hot-metal technology".
notes: Source: https://www.reading.ac.uk/typography/research/research-stories/fiona-ross; https://fontsinuse.com/typefaces/126365/linotype-bengali; F1.21 spec claim 15. Dates probable.

name: Han unification (1992)
making_significance: Unicode gave Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Vietnamese Han characters shared code points, decided by experts from those countries.
notes: Source: https://www.unicode.org/history/publicationdates.html; F1.21 spec claim 16. Two readings, no ruling. links: INS073

name: Etsy rule change (2013)
making_significance: Etsy let sellers hire staff, outsource shipping and use manufacturers if they showed "authorship of the idea".
notes: Source: https://techcrunch.com/2013/10/01/facing-backlash-from-solo-sellers-etsy-changes-policies-to-allow-for-additional-staff-and-manufacturing-support-outsourced-shipping-and-more/; F1.21 spec claim 17. links: INS077

name: Indigo Commission (1860)
making_significance: After the indigo revolt, the commission's report said ryots could not be forced to grow indigo.
leaves_out: the ryots tied by advances and contracts
notes: Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Indigo-Revolt; F1.22 spec claim 11. links: OCC137

name: US wool-tariff removal (1894)
making_significance: After the US removed its wool tariff, "the Navajo blanket was transformed into a rug and weavers' productivity quadrupled"; traders bought weaving by weight.
notes: Source: https://digitalcommons.unl.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1714&context=tsaconf; F1.22a spec claim 13. links: OBT331; PRA035

name: Crimean treasures case (2014–2023)
making_significance: Crimean museums, backed by Russia, and the Ukrainian state both claimed objects on loan in Amsterdam; Dutch courts ruled for Ukraine and the objects went to Kyiv in 2023.
leaves_out: the Crimean museums' staff and Crimean Tatar communities
notes: Source: https://www.hogeraad.nl/actueel/nieuwsoverzicht/2023/juni/beslissing-hof-allard-pierson-museum-krimschatten-afgeven-staat/; https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2021/10/27/crimean-gold-trove-must-return-to-ukraine-not-russia-dutch-court-rules; F1.24 spec claims 8–10. Two readings of where they belong. links: INS138; INS139

name: AAMD 1970 guideline
making_significance: The museums' test asks that an object left its country before, or was legally exported after, 17 November 1970; it passes an object taken in 1897.
defined_by: the Association of Art Museum Directors
notes: Source: https://aamd.org/for-the-media/press-release/strengthened-guidelines-on-the-acquisition-of-archaeological-material; F1.24 spec claim 13.

name: Prada SS26 Kolhapuri case (2025–2026)
making_significance: Prada showed "leather sandals" modelled on the Kolhapuri chappal, then credited the tradition and signed with the GI holders.
leaves_out: the makers, who were not party to the deal
notes: Source: https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/society-equity/prada-launch-930-made-india-sandals-after-backlash-2025-12-11; https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/7/1/why-is-prada-caught-in-a-sandal-scandal-in-india; F1.26 spec claim 17. links: PRA222

name: Haka Ka Mate Attribution Act (2014)
making_significance: The Act requires commercial publications and films of Ka Mate to state that Te Rauparaha composed it; performance and education are exempt, and the only remedy is a declaration.
notes: Source: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2014/0018/latest/whole.html; F1.26 spec claim 11.

name: Frozen 2 agreement (2019)
making_significance: Disney agreed with the Sámi Parliaments and the Saami Council on a North Sámi version, exchanges and a six-member Verddet group.
notes: Source: https://samediggi.fi/en/news/unique-collaboration-gives-impacts-to-sapmi/; https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/frozen-2-consultation-sami-1.5370801; F1.26 spec claims 12–13.

name: Transfers to Ájtte (2023 and 2025)
making_significance: Sweden's National Museums of World Culture transferred 477 objects in 2023 and 64 in 2025 to Ájtte under the Museums Act.
defined_by: the National Museums of World Culture
notes: Source: https://www.varldskulturmuseerna.se/en/collections/return-of-objects-from-the-collections/return-of-sami-objects/; F1.26 spec claim 14. links: INS148

name: San Code of Research Ethics (2017)
making_significance: The San Code of Research Ethics names "respect, honesty, justice and fairness, and care".
notes: Source: https://trust-project.eu/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/San-Code-of-RESEARCH-Ethics-Booklet-final.pdf; F1.26 spec claim 15. Linked, not paraphrased at length. links: INS149

name: Ancestral Voices collection
making_significance: A Library of Congress collection of 31 surviving cylinders recorded at Calais, Maine, in 1890, piloting Traditional Knowledge labels through Mukurtu.
defined_by: the Library of Congress; the Passamaquoddy
notes: Source: https://www.loc.gov/collections/ancestral-voices/about-this-collection/; F1.26 spec claim 16. links: COM308

name: Battle of Talas (751)
making_significance: A battle between Abbasid and Tang forces; the story that captured Chinese papermakers brought paper to Samarkand is a later report that Bloom calls "without factual basis".
defined_by: al-Tha'alibi (11th c., reporting an earlier author); historians
notes: Source: https://archive.org/details/lataif-al-maarif-thaalibi-1968-english; https://edspace.american.edu/silkroadjournal/wp-content/uploads/sites/984/2017/09/Silk-Road-or-Paper-Road.pdf; F1.27 spec claim 5; F1.30a spec claims 1–2. The paper legend is noted as legend. Proposed by F1.27 and F1.30a. links: TEC185; INV037

name: Khotan silk legend
making_significance: A legend that a Chinese princess smuggled mulberry seed and silkworm eggs to Khotan in her head-dress; the event is legend, the text is documented.
notes: Source: https://archive.org/details/siyukibuddhistre02hsuoft; F1.29 spec claims 8–9. Marked "legend".

name: Leonid storm (1833)
making_significance: A meteor storm that winter counts record as "The Year the Stars Fell"; Mallery used it to align counts with Western calendars.
notes: Source: https://americanindian.si.edu/exhibitions/horsenation/wintercount.html; https://museumsandtheweb.com/mw2005/abstracts/prg_280000983.html; F1.30 spec claim 16. links: OBT150

name: Zuni map art (2006–)
making_significance: Zuni artists made map paintings of Zuni places for their own museum, later shown at the Fowler (2015–16); counts differ by date.
notes: Source: http://www.ashiwi-museum.org/exhibitions/; https://fowler.ucla.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Zuni-World_Press-Release_Final-9-22-15.pdf; F1.31 spec claim 14. No map reproduced or described. links: COM099; INS156

name: Safeguarding programme for Al Sadu (2011–2023)
making_significance: The UAE's safeguarding programme for Al Sadu weaving entered UNESCO's Register of Good Safeguarding Practices in 2025, separate from the element.
notes: Source: https://ich.unesco.org/en/BSP/safeguarding-programme-for-al-sadu-traditional-weaving-skills-in-the-united-arab-emirates-02473; F1.31 spec claim 8. links: PRA131; MKR058

name: UNESCO Ethical Principles for Safeguarding Intangible Cultural Heritage (2015)
making_significance: UNESCO's principles say communities "should have the primary role" in safeguarding and their heritage "should not be subject to external judgements of value".
notes: Source: https://ich.unesco.org/en/Decisions/10.COM/15.a; F1.31 spec claim 6.

name: Michael Thonet
making_significance: The furniture maker learned to bend wood in layers and then solid beech with steam and a metal strip; his firm's No. 14 chair was shipped flat in parts.
leaves_out: the Moravian workers: men steamed and bent, women sanded, finished and caned (V&A)
notes: Source: AIC 1999.555 (https://api.artic.edu/api/v1/artworks/154050); V&A, https://www.vam.ac.uk/articles/thonet-and-the-invention-of-bentwood-furniture; F1.1 spec claims 16–17. Austrian privilege for bending glued layers 16 July 1842; solid-wood bending 1855 (V&A) or 1856 (Museum Boppard). links: INS062; TEC137

name: August Thonet
date_note: dates to verify; the AIC gives none of his own (its artist line prints the firm's 1853–1921)
making_significance: Michael Thonet's son designed bentwood chairs for Gebrüder Thonet, such as the AIC side chair of c. 1885 in beech and cane.
leaves_out: the factory workers who made the chairs
notes: Source: AIC 1999.556 (https://api.artic.edu/api/v1/artworks/154051); F1.1 spec claim 15. links: INS062

name: Musli
making_significance: An İznik lamp of 1549 made for the Dome of the Rock names Musli as its decorator, with the date and place of making: a painter's name written where most were not.
leaves_out: the potters, glaze-makers and quartz diggers, not named
free_sources: Museum With No Frontiers (link-out); British Museum (link-out)
notes: Source: https://islamicart.museumwnf.org/database_item.php?id=object;ISL;uk;Mus01;39;en; F1.1 spec claim 14. links: MKR057; PLC305; OBT024

name: Hans and Marie-Louise Erlenmeyer
date_note: fl.; collected between 1943 and the early 1960s; sold at Christie's, London, 13 December 1988
making_significance: The collectors bought proto-cuneiform tablets whose exit from Iraq is not recorded; the Met's tablet passes the 1970 test only on this collection-level statement.
leaves_out: the tablets' findspots and the people who dug them
notes: Source: Met provenance, https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/329081; Englund 2001 (https://cdli.earth/files-up/publications/englund2001b.pdf); F1.1 spec claim 9. A couple; one row.

name: Kehar Singh
date_note: fl. c. 1860, Punjab (probably Amritsar or Lahore)
making_significance: The Company-school painter made Weaving and Spinning, whose inscriptions name him and the occupations shown.
leaves_out: the weavers and spinners shown, who are named only by trade
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1987.162 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1987.162); F1.2 spec claim 3.

name: Giovanni Paolo Panini
making_significance: The painter's views of Rome "were popular with foreigners who visited the city on their Grand Tours": souvenirs at the top of the market.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1974.39 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1974.39); F1.2 spec claim 19.

name: Victor de Riqueti, marquis de Mirabeau
other_names: Victor de Riqueti, marquis de Mirabeau
making_significance: His L'Ami des hommes holds the use of "civilisation" long cited as the earliest in French; recent lexicography reports earlier uses.
leaves_out: the peoples the word was later set against
notes: Source: https://www.persee.fr/doc/barb_0001-4133_1990_num_1_5_22686; F1.3 spec claim 1.

name: Charles Batteux
making_significance: Kristeller (1951) called Batteux's 1746 treatise "the decisive step" towards the modern system of the fine arts, which set crafts apart.
leaves_out: the crafts the system ranked lower
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Batteux (summary); F1.3 spec claim 13. Interpretive: a scholar's thesis.

name: J. Theodore Bent
date_note: died 1897; The Ruined Cities of Mashonaland 1892 (1895 edition)
making_significance: His book credited Great Zimbabwe to "a Semitic race" of "Arabian origin", a claim archaeology later refuted.
leaves_out: the Shona builders of Great Zimbabwe
free_sources: Project Gutenberg (public domain in the USA)
notes: Source: https://www.gutenberg.org/files/69067/69067-h/69067-h.htm; F1.3 spec claim 14. links: PLC087; CIV005

name: Gertrude Caton-Thompson
making_significance: The archaeologist's excavation found Great Zimbabwe to be African work.
notes: Source: https://sas-space.sas.ac.uk/4213/1/Preben_Kaarsholm_-_The_past_as_battlefield_in_Rhodesia_and_Zimbabwe.pdf; F1.3 spec claim 15. links: PLC087

name: Peter Garlake
making_significance: The archaeologist of Great Zimbabwe was forced into exile in 1970 as Rhodesia barred official statements that the site was African.
notes: Source: https://sas-space.sas.ac.uk/4213/1/Preben_Kaarsholm_-_The_past_as_battlefield_in_Rhodesia_and_Zimbabwe.pdf; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/239789630_Peter_Garlake_1934-2011_Great_Zimbabwe_and_the_politics_of_the_past_in_Zimbabwe; F1.3 spec claim 15. links: PLC087

name: Sultan 'Ali al-Mashhadi
making_significance: The calligrapher copied pages of Sa'di and Hafiz in Herat; a Met page shows how such work was later filed as "Islamic art".
notes: Source: Met 11.84.2 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/446169); F1.3 spec §5.

name: Ahmed Ansari
making_significance: A co-author of the Decolonising Design manifesto (2019), which says including more actors in design institutions is "not sufficient".
notes: Source: https://jfsdigital.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/12-Ansari-Decolonising-Design.pdf; F1.3 spec claim 19.

name: James Reese Europe
making_significance: The bandleader's Society Orchestra recorded dance music for Victor in 1913–14, before the ODJB's 1917 disc.
notes: Source: https://www.loc.gov/item/jukebox-134539/; F1.4 spec claim 7.

name: Mamadou Kouyaté
making_significance: The kora maker built an instrument about 1960 that his nephew Djimo Kouyaté later re-bridged and restrung: an instrument never finished.
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/503060; F1.4 spec claim 15.

name: Itti-Marduk-balāṭu
making_significance: The scribe wrote a tablet with a diagram and rules for the Game of Ur, which the British Museum calls the oldest known rules for a board game.
notes: Source: https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/W_Rm-III-6-b; F1.4 spec claim 19.

name: Wang Chaohui
making_significance: A national inheritor of wooden movable-type printing in Dongyuan, Rui'an: "The family tree records everything about your ancestors."
notes: Source: https://news.cgtn.com/news/3d3d514d77496a4e33457a6333566d54/index.html; F1.5 spec claim 25. Consent route not yet established (F1.5 spec §2). links: PRA078

name: Ahammangiwa (Igueghae)
date_note: fl.; 13th century in one Benin court oral history
making_significance: One of many Benin court oral histories says this foreign artisan brought lost-wax casting to Benin; other accounts point to Ife.
defined_by: Benin court oral history, as the Met reports it
leaves_out: the Igun Eronmwon who carried the craft
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/perspectives/bronze-casters-igun-street; F1.6 spec claim 11. Oral history: one account among several. links: MKR001; PLC037

name: Paul B. Travis
making_significance: The Cleveland teacher collected carvings in the Belgian Congo in 1927–28 for the Gilpin Players and the African Art Sponsors.
leaves_out: the makers and owners of what he collected
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1929.364 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1929.364); F1.2 spec claim 7. links: INS096; PLC423

name: Johannes van Keulen
making_significance: The Amsterdam chart firm published a sea chart of the Bight of Benin drawn by Jan Luyken: it maps the route the brass came by, not the people who cast it.
leaves_out: the people of the coast it charted
notes: Source: Rijksmuseum RP-P-1896-A-19368-3110 (https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/RP-P-1896-A-19368-3110); F1.6 spec claim 18.

name: Asdzáá Tl'ógí (Juanita)
making_significance: NMNH presumes, from two photographs of 1874, that she wove on the loom brought to Washington with the 1874 Diné delegation.
defined_by: NMNH ("Juanita is presumed to be the weaver")
notes: Source: https://www.si.edu/object/nmnhanthropology_8345504; F1.7 spec claim 24. Record spelling Asdzáá Tl'ógí. links: COM097; PRA035

name: Julio C. Tello
making_significance: His team excavated at Paracas and located the Necrópolis de Wari Kayan in 1927.
notes: Source: https://traffickingculture.org/encyclopedia/case-studies/paracas-textiles/; F1.7 spec claim 4. links: ARC205

name: Sven Karell
making_significance: The Swedish consul removed Paracas textiles illegally; Gothenburg returned them to Peru in 2014, 2017 and 2021.
leaves_out: the Paracas weavers and their descendants
notes: Source: https://traffickingculture.org/encyclopedia/case-studies/paracas-textiles/; https://www.elperuano.pe/noticia/124707-peru-recibe-los-ultimos-textiles-de-la-cultura-paracas-que-se-encontraban-en-suecia; F1.24 spec claim 14; F1.7 spec §10.

name: Langdon Warner
date_note: bought Goryeo celadon in Korea for Cleveland, 1918
making_significance: The American curator bought Goryeo celadon, given to Cleveland in 1918; no findspot is recorded.
leaves_out: the tombs the celadon came from
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1918.471 and 1918.458 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1918.458); F1.8 spec claim 9.

name: Jean Theodore Royer
making_significance: The Hague collector owned an Arita bottle enamelled in the Netherlands, later passed to William I and the Rijksmuseum.
notes: Source: Rijksmuseum AK-NM-6464-A; F1.8 spec claim 19.

name: Subhash Kapoor
making_significance: The New York dealer sold the Sripuranthan Nataraja; a Kumbakonam court convicted him over 19 idols in 2022.
notes: Source: https://news.artnet.com/art-world-archives/subhash-kapoor-ten-year-sentence-2202695; F1.9 spec claim 15. Living person, named as a convicted public figure; whether the conviction includes Sripuranthan is not stated.

name: Mithra
making_significance: A painter in Akbar's atelier; the Met attributes a Hamzanama folio to Dasavanta and Mithra.
materials_techniques: opaque watercolour and gold on cloth
notes: Source: Met 24.48.1 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/447752); F1.9 spec claim 11. links: PER233; MKR044

name: Nanni
making_significance: His letter to Ea-nasir complains that the wrong grade of copper ore was delivered after a Gulf voyage.
notes: Source: BM 131236 (https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/W_1953-0411-71); F1.9a spec claim 10.

name: Beshir Agha
making_significance: He was "enslaved in his native Ethiopia as a boy"; as chief harem eunuch he founded libraries that "helped to shape" the Ottoman state's intellectual profile.
notes: Source: https://nes.princeton.edu/publications/beshir-agha-chief-eunuch-ottoman-imperial-harem; Walters W.591; F1.10 spec claims 9–10. links: POL241; INS044

name: Philippe-Joseph Brocard
making_significance: The Paris glassmaker "produced many lamp reproductions" in Mamluk style; Cleveland says its lamp may be by him.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1981.10 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1981.10); F1.10 spec claim 20. links: STY182; TEC049

name: Muhammad ibn Qala'un
making_significance: The Mamluk sultan named on a European bottle of c. 1900 that imitates Mamluk glass.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1944.488 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1944.488); F1.10 spec claim 20. Reign dates not in the spec. links: POL042

name: Yushaa Abdullah
date_note: living; studied with Hasan Çelebi from December 2007
making_significance: A calligrapher in Nigeria who studied with Hasan Çelebi through IRCICA.
notes: Source: https://www.scriptsnscribes.com/blogs/2021/8/13/a-conversation-with-master-calligrapher-yushaa-abdullah; F1.10 spec claim 23. Linked, not quoted, until the consent route is used (AR-062).

name: Hasan Çelebi
making_significance: The Istanbul calligrapher teaches students from many countries, among them Yushaa Abdullah from December 2007.
notes: Source: https://www.scriptsnscribes.com/blogs/2021/8/13/a-conversation-with-master-calligrapher-yushaa-abdullah; F1.10 spec claim 23.

name: Johann Philipp Raab
making_significance: The Mainz joiner made a writing cabinet in 1764 as his masterpiece; its drawing and description were part of the master's examination, after which he joined the joiners' guild.
notes: Source: https://www.deutsche-digitale-bibliothek.de/item/IMT25HT6PFDQSUBD3VPQNY2L6UDIFISJ; F1.11 spec claim 17. links: MKR095; INS113

name: Jan Luyken
making_significance: With his son Caspar he etched the hundred trade prints of Het Menselyk Bedryf (1694), among them the papermaker and the printer.
