notes: Source: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/RP-P-OB-44.516; F1.11 spec claim 15. links: PER516

name: Caspar Luyken
making_significance: Etched the trade prints of Het Menselyk Bedryf (1694) with his father Jan.
notes: Source: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/RP-P-OB-44.516; F1.11 spec claim 15. links: PER515

name: Utilis of Lyon
making_significance: A red-gloss potter of Lyon known from a stamp on a bowl found at a Roman fort at Nijmegen; the holder notes a name common among enslaved people on its graffito.
leaves_out: the enslaved and freed workers of the workshops
notes: Source: Valkhof PDB.1998.2.KH.295.126 (https://www.europeana.eu/item/2021648/resource_document_collectiegelderland_XXBHEMPND7ZQSYE5DNJS4NDABQICFG5BLNBMJB2OFRUNWJFKW24Q); F1.11 spec claim 7. links: TEC041; PLC450

name: Lydos
date_note: Archaic Athens; dates not given in the spec
making_significance: An Athenian painter who signed two vases "the Lydian": a Lydian who came to Athens or a son of Lydian parents; whether he was free is not recorded.
notes: Source: https://collections.louvre.fr/en/ark:/53355/cl010269703; F1.11 spec claim 4.

name: Amasis
making_significance: A potter's signature, Amasis, gives the modern name "Amasis Painter" to the painter of a lekythos showing women weaving, weighing and spinning wool.
leaves_out: the women at the loom shown, unnamed
notes: Source: Met 31.11.10 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/253348); F1.11 spec claim 3.

name: Étienne Boileau
making_significance: The Livre des métiers, rules for Paris trades, was compiled under the provost, most likely 1266–69; the 101 trade titles are the 19th-century editors' attribution.
leaves_out: the silk spinners and other women's trades it lists
notes: Source: https://journals.openedition.org/medievales/7569; F1.11 spec claim 10.

name: Otto Meyer
making_significance: The missionary dug Lapita sherds on Wuatam Island in German New Guinea; how they left the colony is not recorded.
notes: Source: https://collections.museumsvictoria.com.au/api/items/187023; F1.12 spec claim 12.

name: Dermot A. Casey
making_significance: The archaeologist's photograph "Wuatam (Watom) Island Pottery" is in Museums Victoria, marked public domain.
notes: Source: https://collections.museumsvictoria.com.au/api/articles/16808; F1.12 spec §5.

name: Nainoa Thompson
making_significance: In 1980 he repeated the voyage to Tahiti and navigated home, which PVS calls "a feat that hadn't been accomplished in 600 years".
notes: Source: https://hokulea.com/history/; F1.12 spec claim 19. As PVS's claim. links: PRA197; INS117

name: Kamanaʻopono Crabbe
making_significance: Writing for OHA in 2017, he credited Mau Piailug with leading the 1976 voyage that "helped Hawaiians reclaim our voyaging traditions".
notes: Source: https://kawaiola.news/oha/ceo/ceo201707/; F1.12 spec claim 18. links: PER344; PRA197

name: Konstantin von Kaufman
making_significance: As governor-general of Russian Turkestan he commissioned the Turkestan Album (1871–72; about 1,200 photographs).
notes: Source: https://guides.loc.gov/turkestan-album; F1.12a spec claim 20.

name: A. L. Kun
making_significance: Compiled the ethnographic part of the Turkestan Album with N. N. Nekhoroshev.
notes: Source: https://guides.loc.gov/turkestan-album; F1.12a spec §6.

name: Han Gan
making_significance: The Tang painter's Night-Shining White shows Emperor Xuanzong's horse, a Central Asian "celestial steed".
notes: Source: Met 1977.78 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/39901); F1.12a spec claim 16.

name: Cresques Abraham
making_significance: The Majorcan mapmaker is credited with the Catalan Atlas, which shows Mansa Musa as "the richest" ruler of Guinea.
notes: Source: https://essentiels.bnf.fr/fr/image/0ce33594-50b3-4c79-9986-116699f7c942-nomade-afrique-et-seigneur-guinee; F1.13 spec claim 13. Attributed. links: OCC037

name: Omar ibn Said
making_significance: Born in Futa Toro, captured in 1807 and enslaved in South Carolina, he wrote his life in Arabic in 1831.
notes: Source: https://www.loc.gov/item/2018371864/; https://docsouth.unc.edu/nc/omarsaid/omarsaid.html; F1.13 spec claim 22. Lead with his name and Arabic text, not the title page's enslaver framing (F1.13 spec §2).

name: Ehrenfried Walther von Tschirnhaus
making_significance: With Böttger he worked out European hard-paste porcelain in Dresden; the date is contested (late 1707, October 1708 or 1709).
leaves_out: Böttger's assistants Paul Wildenstein and David Köhler
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/german-and-austrian-porcelain-in-the-eighteenth-century; https://www.seaceramic.org.sg/wp-content/uploads/European-Discovery-of-Porcelain_Rinaldi.pdf; F1.14 spec claim 12. links: PER402

name: Oswald Brierly
making_significance: The voyage artist brought a Tongan dress to Owen Jones, who reported that one woman designed all the island's patterns.
leaves_out: the woman designer, whose name is not recorded
notes: Source: Owen Jones, Grammar of Ornament (1856), AS-001; F1.15 spec claim 4. links: OBT047; COM291

name: Empress Shōtoku (Kōken)
making_significance: She ordered the One Million Pagodas after her court suppressed the Emi rebellion of 764 and sent them to major temples.
notes: Source: Met 30.47a–c (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/44955); F1.16 spec claim 4. links: OBT326; OCC306

name: Wang Jie
making_significance: His colophon on the Diamond Sutra, the earliest known dated printed book, says it was "reverently made for universal free distribution … on behalf of his two parents"; the block cutter is unnamed.
notes: Source: https://idp.bl.uk/blog/the-diamond-sutra-on-display-text-panel-6-with-colophon/; F1.16 spec claim 2. links: PLC188; INV039

name: Mvemba a Nzinga (Afonso I of Kongo)
making_significance: In the early 1500s the Kongo king made Catholicism the state religion and sponsored Christian art, made by Kongo artists.
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/318323; https://news.yale.edu/2019/03/05/art-historian-cecile-fromont-uncovers-kongos-christian-visual-culture; F1.16 spec claim 8. The sources name "the Kongo king"; the own name Mvemba a Nzinga is standard but not in the spec. links: GAP054; POL020

name: Pedro de Gante
making_significance: The Franciscan "likely supervised" the feather Mass of St Gregory (1539), made by an Indigenous artist.
notes: Source: https://smarthistory.org/featherworks/; F1.16 spec claim 14. Probable supervisor, not maker. links: MKR019; TEC109

name: Domenico Ghirlandaio
making_significance: With his brother David he contracted with Giovanni Tornabuoni in 1485 to paint the choir of Santa Maria Novella; the contract fixed the blue and the gold.
notes: Source: Davies, Ghirlandaio (1909), App. VI, https://archive.org/details/ghirlandaio00daviuoft; F1.17 spec claim 3. links: PER537; PER538

name: David Ghirlandaio
making_significance: Engaged with his brother Domenico under the 1485 Tornabuoni contract for the Santa Maria Novella choir.
notes: Source: https://archive.org/details/ghirlandaio00daviuoft; F1.17 spec claim 3.

name: Giovanni Tornabuoni
making_significance: The Florentine patron contracted the Ghirlandaio brothers in 1485, naming "azzurro ultramarino" where needed, fine gold, and the buildings, hills and animals to be shown.
notes: Source: https://archive.org/details/ghirlandaio00daviuoft; https://resources.warburg.sas.ac.uk/pdf/cna750b2242783.pdf; F1.17 spec claim 3 and §10.

name: Paul de Lamerie
making_significance: Born in 's-Hertogenbosch of Huguenot parents, the London goldsmith was apprenticed to Pierre Platel and entered the Goldsmiths' livery in 1717.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/term/BIOG82192; Cleveland 1943.179; F1.17 spec claims 10–11. links: DIA010; MKR062

name: Onijagbo Obasoro Alowolodu
making_significance: The Ogoga (king) of Ikere commissioned Olowe of Ise's veranda post for his palace, c. 1910–14.
notes: Source: AIC 1984.550 (https://api.artic.edu/api/v1/artworks/102611); F1.17 spec claim 13. links: PER014; PLC459

name: Santana Roybal Martinez
making_significance: The San Ildefonso potter painted with her mother-in-law Maria Martinez; plates of c. 1943–51 are signed "Marie and Santana".
notes: Source: Cleveland 1951.363 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1951.363); F1.18 spec claim 16. links: PER108; COM100

name: Popovi Da
making_significance: Maria Martinez's son; pots from 1956 are signed "Maria/Popovi".
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Martinez; F1.18 spec claim 15. Probable. links: PER108

name: Michel-Marie Carquillat
making_significance: The Lyon weaver wove the silk portrait of Jacquard (1839) on more than 24,000 cards, for Didier, Petit et Cie.
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/222531; F1.19 spec claims 12–13. links: INS121; MKR075

name: Claude Bonnefond
making_significance: His 1831 portrait of Jacquard, commissioned by the city of Lyon, was the model for the woven silk portrait.
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/222531; F1.19 spec claim 13.

name: Charles Babbage
making_significance: Babbage took the Jacquard mechanism as a model for his Analytical Engine.
notes: Source: https://www.sciencehistory.org/stories/magazine/the-french-connection/; F1.19 spec claim 12. Whether he owned the woven portrait is unverified. links: PER412

name: Hayashi Kodenji
making_significance: The Nagoya cloisonné maker is credited with a drum made "by order of the Japanese government for the Vienna Exposition of 1873".
notes: Source: Met 89.4.1236a–d (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/501802); F1.19 spec claim 19. Name order: Japanese order Hayashi Kodenji. links: EVT002

name: Gottfried Wagener
making_significance: The German adviser steered Japan's Vienna 1873 selection towards "delicately created industrial art products" rather than machinery.
notes: Source: https://www.ndl.go.jp/exposition/e/s1/1873-2.html; F1.19 spec claim 18. links: EVT002

name: Sakura Tsuneshichi
making_significance: One of three Kyoto weavers sent to Lyon in 1872, who brought back "jacquards and battant" to Nishijin.
notes: Source: https://www.ndl.go.jp/france/en/part1/s2_2.html; F1.19 spec claim 16.

name: Paul Brunat
making_significance: The French technical director under whom Tomioka Silk Mill began in 1872, training young women who took reeling skills home.
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1449/; F1.19 spec claim 17.

name: Brown Fleming
making_significance: The Scottish trader took Haarlem wax prints to the Gold Coast, where women traders were central to the market.
notes: Source: https://api.taylorfrancis.com/content/chapters/oa-edit/download?identifierName=doi&identifierValue=10.4324%2F9780429295607-6&type=chapterpdf; F1.19 spec claim 20. links: INS124

name: Guillaume Boucher
making_significance: The Paris goldsmith, captured in Hungary and taken to Karakorum, made a great silver tree whose lions poured mare's milk; Rubruck heard of him.
leaves_out: the other captive artisans at Karakorum
notes: Source: Rubruck (Rockhill 1900), https://archive.org/stream/journeyofwilliam00ruys/journeyofwilliam00ruys_djvu.txt; F1.19a spec claims 2–3; F1.23 spec. Where he was taken is contested. Proposed by F1.19a, F1.23 and F1.28. links: PLC258

name: Cosmas the Ruthenian
date_note: met by Carpini at the Mongol court
making_significance: Carpini met "a certain Ruthenian called Cosmas, a goldsmith", who made Güyük's throne and seal.
notes: Source: https://depts.washington.edu/silkroad/texts/carpini.html; F1.19a spec claim 4. links: PLC258

name: Norman Wilkinson
making_significance: The marine painter proposed painting ships "to break up her form"; his unit drew a scheme for each ship, and over 2,300 were painted by 1918.
leaves_out: the 11 women art students and the dockyard painters
notes: Source: https://daily.jstor.org/the-camouflage-that-dazzled; https://unwritten-record.blogs.archives.gov/?p=17206; F1.19a spec claim 11. links: OCC189

name: Bhai Ram Singh
making_significance: Trained as a carpenter, he became Vice-Principal of the Mayo School and was commissioned "to design the decoration" of the Durbar Room at Osborne.
notes: Source: https://www.rct.uk/collection/403750/bhai-ram-singh; https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/places/osborne/things-to-do/state-rooms; F1.19b spec claim 10. Credit contested: English Heritage's own page credits Kipling and Ram Singh. links: PER241; INS128

name: Youssef Kamal
making_significance: The prince founded and endowed the Egyptian School of Fine Arts in Cairo (1908), free of charge.
notes: Source: https://finearts.capu.edu.eg/en/about-en/history-of-the-faculty; F1.19b spec claim 18. links: INS129

name: Kano Tan'yū
making_significance: The Kano painter's 1666 sketch of Mi Fu may be a record copy (shukuzu) or a design for a painting; the Met gives both readings.
notes: Source: Met 1996.464.1 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/44297); F1.19b spec claim 2. links: SCH040; OBT349

name: Wang Gai
making_significance: Illustrated the Mustard Seed Garden Manual by adapting an earlier primer, giving painters without a collection "a glimpse into the elite training".
notes: Source: Met CP6 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/63185); F1.19b spec claim 3.

name: Inge Scholl
making_significance: Co-founded the HfG Ulm in 1953 with Otl Aicher and Max Bill.
notes: Source: https://hfg-archiv.museumulm.de/en/the-hfg-archive/; F1.19b spec claim 15. links: INS060; PLC343

name: Otl Aicher
making_significance: Co-founded the HfG Ulm in 1953 with Inge Scholl and Max Bill.
notes: Source: https://hfg-archiv.museumulm.de/en/the-hfg-archive/; F1.19b spec claim 15. links: INS060

name: Max Bill
making_significance: Co-founded the HfG Ulm in 1953; it taught from 1955 to 1968 and was a model for schools in India and Brazil.
notes: Source: https://hfg-archiv.museumulm.de/en/the-hfg-archive/; F1.19b spec claim 15. links: INS060

name: Jerónimo Antonio Gil
making_significance: The engraver led the Academy of San Carlos in Mexico City, described as "the earliest art academy in the Americas", where students drew from plaster casts.
notes: Source: https://smarthistory.org/the-academy-of-san-carlos/; F1.19b spec claim 20. links: INS011

name: Paul Klee
making_significance: The painter made the lithograph Tightrope Walker (1923) while on the Bauhaus faculty.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1961.154 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1961.154); F1.20 spec §5 and §10. Cleveland does not say the print was made or published at the Bauhaus. links: INS057

name: Usto Shirin Muradov
making_significance: Uzbekistan's heritage list names him a leading ganch carver of the Navoi Theatre's decoration.
notes: Source: http://ich.uz/en/ich-of-uzbekistan/national-list/domain-5/441-ganchkorlik; F1.20 spec claim 7. Second source still sought.

name: Eulie Chowdhury
making_significance: V&A captions credit the Indian architect as designer of a V-leg officer's chair and co-designer of a library chair for Chandigarh; the Met credits Jeanneret.
notes: Source: https://theconversation.com/tropical-modernism-architecture-and-independence-at-vanda-reintroduces-indian-and-ghanaian-pioneers-of-the-style-224556; https://human.libretexts.org/Courses/City_College_of_San_Francisco/A_History_of_Designed_Interiors/10%3A_Modern_Design/10.02%3A_Modern_Chair_Design_1920s-1960s/10.2.03%3A_The_Chandigarh_Chair; F1.20 spec claim 15 and §10. Maker credit contested. links: OBT353; PER255

name: John Owusu-Addo
making_significance: The Ghanaian architect returned to teach at KNUST after training abroad, in the V&A's account of tropical modernism.
notes: Source: https://www.vam.ac.uk/articles/about-the-tropical-modernism-exhibition; F1.20 spec claim 14.

name: Lúcio Costa
making_significance: The planner drew the plan of Brasília with Oscar Niemeyer.
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/445/; F1.20 spec claim 17. links: PLC472

name: Marguerite Boucicaut
making_significance: She ran Le Bon Marché after Aristide Boucicaut's death; the credit usually goes to him.
notes: Source: https://fashionheritage.eu/le-bon-marche; F1.21 spec claim 3. links: INS134

name: Charles Frederick Worth
making_significance: After working at Gagelin he opened his own house in 1858, showed designs on live models and sewed his name into garments.
leaves_out: the seamstresses and embroiderers, over 1,200 staff
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/charles-frederick-worth-1825-1895-and-the-house-of-worth; F1.21 spec claims 5–6. "Earliest designer label" is to check. links: GAP072

name: Torii Kiyonaga
making_significance: The print designer showed the Echigoya on New Year's Day in a triptych.
notes: Source: AIC 1930.382 (https://www.artic.edu/artworks/86454); F1.21 spec claim 1. links: STY148

name: Jules Chéret
making_significance: The poster artist's colour lithographs, such as Saxoleine (1893), were printed by Imprimerie Chaix.
notes: Source: AIC 2013.1144 (https://www.artic.edu/artworks/218855); F1.21 spec §5. links: OBT135; TEC194

name: Alexandre Lunois
making_significance: His print The Fancy Goods Store (1902) depicts Le Bon Marché, Cleveland says.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 2012.288 (https://clevelandart.org/art/2012.288); F1.21 spec §5. links: INS134

name: Cal Stewart
making_significance: He wrote and spoke the comic monologue "Uncle Josh Weathersby in a department store" (Victor 665).
notes: Source: https://adp.library.ucsb.edu/index.php/matrix/detail/2000000228/Pre-matrix_B-665-Uncle_Josh_Weathersby_in_a_department_store; F1.21 spec claim 8.

name: Kaderdina Hajee Essak
making_significance: The Mombasa merchant is credited with printing words on kanga, at his wife's suggestion.
leaves_out: his wife, whose idea it was, unnamed
notes: Source: https://www.aramcoworld.com/articles/2017/kangas-woven-voices; F1.21 spec claim 11. Probable. links: OBT042

name: Ottmar Mergenthaler
date_note: fl.; Linotype in commercial use July 1886
making_significance: His Linotype went into commercial use at the New York Tribune in July 1886, the earliest known installation, casting whole lines from molten metal.
notes: Source: https://www.printmuseum.org/1895-linotype; F1.21 spec claim 12. The claim names the machine, not the inventor; his role is standard. links: GAP028

name: Kamel Mrowa
making_significance: The founder of Al-Hayat in Beirut approached Linotype in 1954, leading to Simplified Arabic, which cut the character count to fit one magazine.
leaves_out: the calligraphers whose letterforms were cut
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Arabic; F1.21 spec claim 13. links: OCC326; STY114

name: Wang Xuan
making_significance: He stored Chinese characters as outlines and parametric strokes for laser typesetting under Project 748.
notes: Source: https://newsen.pku.edu.cn/news_events/news/people/8889.html; https://tsaf.cas.cn/en/hj/kxj/year/1990/201006/t20100607_4954628.html; F1.21 spec claim 14. links: PER577; OCC327

name: Chen Kunqiu
making_significance: She designed and built the large-scale software of the Chinese laser typesetting system; the credit usually goes to Wang Xuan.
notes: Source: https://newsen.pku.edu.cn/news_events/news/people/8889.html; F1.21 spec claim 14. links: PER576

name: Henry De Witt Moulton
making_significance: Credited with "The Great Heap", a photograph of guano on the Chincha Islands (Alexander Gardner is also named).
notes: Source: https://digitalcollections.nypl.org/items/ab4769e0-c61a-012f-0974-58d385a7bc34; F1.22 spec §5. Whether Gardner or Moulton made plate 45 is unverified.

name: Itō Tōgai
making_significance: The scholar's 1727 record tells how the Bakōhan bowl was sent to China for a replacement and came back clamped.
notes: Source: https://emuseum.nich.go.jp/detail?content_base_id=100886&langId=en; F1.22a spec claim 5. links: TEC237

name: P. K. Sethi
making_significance: The surgeon developed the Jaipur foot with the craftsman Ram Chandra Sharma.
notes: Source: https://blog.sciencemuseum.org.uk/jaipur-foot-the-low-cost-prosthetic-that-revolutionised-medical-care-in-india-and-beyond/; F1.22a spec claim 19. Dates not verified.

name: Ram Chandra Sharma
making_significance: "A craftsman at the hospital" who made the Jaipur foot with P. K. Sethi and "received little credit … largely due to his low social status".
notes: Source: https://blog.sciencemuseum.org.uk/jaipur-foot-the-low-cost-prosthetic-that-revolutionised-medical-care-in-india-and-beyond/; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11480697; F1.22a spec claim 19. Dates not verified.

name: Amennakht
making_significance: The scribe of the tomb wrote the Strike Papyrus, recording the crew's cry "we are hungry!" after 18 days without rations.
notes: Source: Turin Cat. 1880 (https://collezioni.museoegizio.it/en-GB/material/Cat_1880); F1.23 spec claim 9. Year 29 given as an approximate CE date; whether he is the Amennakht of Met stela 21.2.6 is not settled. links: MKR090; DYN005

name: Francis Greenway
making_significance: The convict architect designed the Hyde Park Barracks, built by convicts.
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1306/; F1.23 spec claim 15. links: PLC479

name: Judith Scott
making_significance: Born with Down syndrome and largely deaf, she made fibre sculptures at Creative Growth from 1987, shown in a 2014 Brooklyn retrospective.
notes: Source: https://www.brooklynmuseum.org/exhibitions/judith_scott; F1.23 spec claim 19. links: INS136

name: Ralph Moor
making_significance: The British official sent Benin objects to England after the 1897 invasion, as Cleveland's provenance records.
leaves_out: the Igun Eronmwon and the Benin court
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1999.1 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/?q=1999.1&cc0=1); F1.24 spec claim 2. links: OCC175

name: Sydney Burney
making_significance: The dealer sold Benin pieces "as sales agent for the British Museum" around 1950.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1999.1 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/?q=1999.1&cc0=1); F1.24 spec claim 2. links: OCC175

name: Te Rauparaha
making_significance: The chief of Ngāti Toa Rangatira whom the law names as the composer of Ka Mate.
notes: Source: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2014/0018/latest/whole.html; F1.26 spec claim 11.

name: Miwnay
making_significance: A Sogdian woman who wrote Letter 3 of the Ancient Letters to the husband who had left her "destitute".
notes: Source: https://sogdians.si.edu/ancient-letters/; https://idp.bl.uk/collection/21B7971EF80B4C37B654D88A40D3A556/; F1.27 spec claim 3. links: DIA001; CIV088

name: al-Tha'alibi
making_significance: In his Laṭāʾif al-maʿārif he reports, from an earlier author, that Chinese prisoners made paper at Samarkand: the source of the Talas legend.
notes: Source: https://archive.org/details/lataif-al-maarif-thaalibi-1968-english; F1.27 spec claim 5. links: OCC341

name: Ali ibn Shadhan al-Razi
making_significance: He copied "the oldest dated copy of the Quran transcribed on paper", probably in Iran.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Bloom (as for Panjakent); Cleveland 1933.488; F1.27 spec claim 7.

name: William of Rubruck
making_significance: The Flemish Franciscan travelled to the Mongol court and wrote of Karakorum's artisans and Guillaume Boucher's silver tree.
free_sources: Library of Congress; Silk Road Seattle (link-out)
notes: Source: https://depts.washington.edu/silkroad/texts/rubruck.html; https://www.loc.gov/item/01019024/; F1.28 spec claim 2. links: PLC258; PER551

name: Henry Wotton
making_significance: His English version of Vitruvius reordered the triad as "Commoditie, Firmenes, and Delight".
notes: Source: https://archive.org/details/architectureelem00wott; F1.28 spec claim 11. links: TXT001

name: Joseph Gwilt
making_significance: Translated Vitruvius (1826) as "strength, utility, and beauty".
notes: Source: https://lexundria.com/vitr/1.3.2/cf; F1.28 spec claim 12. links: TXT001

name: Morris Hicky Morgan
making_significance: His Vitruvius translation (Harvard, 1914) renders the triad "durability, convenience, and beauty".
free_sources: Project Gutenberg (public domain in the USA)
notes: Source: https://www.gutenberg.org/files/20239/20239-h/20239-h.htm; F1.28 spec claim 12. links: TXT001

name: Tu Shaokui
making_significance: He funded Song Yingxing's Tiangong kaiwu (1637), with 121 illustrations of over 130 technologies.
notes: Source: https://www.loc.gov/item/2021666134/; F1.28 spec claim 17. links: PER167; TXT093

name: Peter R. Schmidt
making_significance: The archaeologist worked with Haya elders on smelts in the 1970s and argued for early preheated furnaces; he later called the smelts "interactive performances".
notes: Source: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1126/science.201.4361.1085; https://archaeologydataservice.ac.uk/archives/view/assemblage/html/4/4schmidt.html; F1.28a spec claims 10–11. Living person (named in the spec). links: TEC072; COM068

name: Pamela H. Smith
making_significance: The historian leads the Making and Knowing Project and translates its manuscript's recipes.
notes: Source: https://the-past.com/feature/secrets-of-their-craft/; F1.28a spec claim 5. links: INS150

name: Xuanzang
making_significance: The monk's record tells how a Chinese princess hid mulberry seed and silkworm eggs in her head-dress for Khotan.
notes: Source: https://archive.org/details/siyukibuddhistre02hsuoft; F1.29 spec claim 8. links: TXT085; OCC342

name: Liang Kai
making_significance: Cleveland attributes to him a scroll picturing silk making in 14 steps, after Lou Shou's Pictures of Tilling and Weaving.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1977.5 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1977.5); F1.29 spec claim 10.

name: Lou Shou
making_significance: His Pictures of Tilling and Weaving is the earliest recorded painting of its genre.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1977.5 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1977.5); F1.29 spec claim 10. Cleveland says "the first recorded"; we say earliest recorded.

name: Rene Orchiston
making_significance: She donated the national collection of 50 harakeke varieties "selected long ago … by Māori weavers".
leaves_out: the Māori weavers who selected the varieties
notes: Source: https://www.landcareresearch.co.nz/resources/collections/harakeke/rene-orchiston-collection-catalogue; F1.29 spec claim 15. links: INS152; MAT073

name: Lynette Youson
making_significance: The Gullah basket maker learned at five from her great-grandmother to coil a rice fanner.
notes: Source: https://americanart.si.edu/artwork/gullah-fanner-basket-82599; F1.29 spec claim 11. links: COM115; OBT364

name: 'Umar ibn Yusuf
making_significance: The Rasulid prince made the Met's astrolabe and wrote a treatise on making astrolabes.
notes: Source: Met 91.1.535a–h (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/444408); F1.30 spec claim 3. links: DYN020

name: Muhammad Zaman
making_significance: The Mashhad instrument maker signed a planispheric astrolabe dated 1065 AH.
notes: Source: Met 63.166a–j (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/451699); F1.30 spec claim 4.

name: Omar Khayyam
making_significance: Among the astronomers who advised on the Jalali calendar adopted in 1079.
notes: Source: https://www.fourmilab.ch/documents/calendar/; F1.30 spec claim 5. links: PRD223

name: Mahmud al-Kashgari
making_significance: His Dīwān Lughāt al-Turk tells of a khagan who named the years after twelve animals.
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C4%ABw%C4%81n_Lugh%C4%81t_al-Turk; F1.30 spec claim 9. links: PRD226

name: Garrick Mallery
date_note: matched the 1833 Leonid storm to winter counts; his own dates not in the spec
making_significance: The ethnologist matched winter counts' "The Year the Stars Fell" to the 1833 Leonid storm.
notes: Source: https://museumsandtheweb.com/mw2005/abstracts/prg_280000983.html; F1.30 spec claim 16. links: OBT150; OCC343

name: Meghnad Saha
making_significance: The physicist headed the Calendar Reform Committee behind India's national calendar (1957).
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_national_calendar; F1.30 spec claim 10. His role rests on the summary. links: PRD229

name: James Mill
making_significance: He split India's past into Hindu, Muslim and British periods by rulers' religion, without going to India; Romila Thapar says this caused distortion.
leaves_out: the makers whose work his periods mislabel
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_History_of_British_India; F1.30 spec claim 20. links: PRD152

name: Koryčany Thonet factory
making_significance: Thonet sited a bentwood factory in the Moravian forests, close to beech, "cheap labour" and rail links.
leaves_out: the workers, men bending and women finishing and caning
notes: Source: https://www.korycany.knihovna.cz/osobnosti/michael-thonet/ (Koryčany town library); V&A (as for Michael Thonet); F1.1 spec claim 17. links: INS062; TEC137

name: Dome of the Rock
date_note: built 691–92 (standard date); İznik lamp made for it 1549
making_significance: The shrine received furnishings from Ottoman workshops, among them an İznik lamp of 1549 that names its decorator.
leaves_out: the makers of its furnishings, mostly unnamed
notes: Source: https://islamicart.museumwnf.org/database_item.php?id=object;ISL;uk;Mus01;39;en; F1.1 spec claim 14. The lamp carries Qur'anic text: link-out only, never cropped (F1.1 spec §2).

name: Santa María Tlahuitoltepec
making_significance: An Ayuujk town in Oaxaca whose embroidered blouse was at the centre of a 2015 copying dispute; its authorities spoke for the community.
notes: Source: https://www.viveoaxaca.org/2015/06/PronunciamientoTlahuitoltepecPlagio2015.html; F1.2 spec claim 17. Ayuujk own name of the town not given in the spec. links: COM124

name: Ekibondo
making_significance: A carver in Ekibondo, then in the Belgian Congo, made an ivory "Elephant Bridge" for European and American buyers from an Asian composition.
leaves_out: the carver, not named; whether Mangbetu carvers made it is not shown
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1929.342 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1929.342); F1.2 spec claims 5, 7. A 1928 checklist reads "Mangbettu, Ekibondis Village": a collector's label, not evidence of the carver (F1.2 spec §4).

name: Black Maria
making_significance: Edison's film studio at West Orange, where Blacksmith Scene was shot in 1893.
notes: Source: https://www.filmpreservation.org/preserved-films/screening-room/blacksmithing-scene-1893; F1.4 spec claim 1.

name: Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company works, Pittsburgh
making_significance: G. W. Bitzer filmed the works for the 1904 St. Louis fair, showing factory making to the public.
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westinghouse_Works; F1.4 spec claim 3.

name: Khedivial Opera House
making_significance: Isma'il Pasha commissioned Aida for the house; Verdi set his fee at 150,000 francs.
notes: Source: https://www.metopera.org/discover/education/educator-guides/aida/the-operas-plot-and-creation/; F1.4 spec claim 10.

name: Abydos tomb U-j
making_significance: Bone and ivory labels from an elite tomb carry some of the earliest known Egyptian signs; Kahl finds the system fully developed only centuries later.
notes: Source: https://www.persee.fr/doc/arnil_1161-0492_2001_num_11_1_1240; F1.5 spec claim 3. Grave goods: link-out with content note. links: INV002

name: Ounjougou
making_significance: Pottery was made here before 9400 BCE; nothing known connects it to China's early pottery.
notes: Source: Huysecom et al. 2009, Antiquity (record: https://vigipallia.parlons-fin-de-vie.fr/Default/doc/OAI_1/oai-HAL-hal-00692506v1/the-emergence-of-pottery-in-africa-during-the-10th-millennium-calbc-new-evidence-from-ounjougou-mali); F1.5 spec claim 9. links: INV022

name: Jiskairumoko
making_significance: Gold cold-hammered into beads, found in a burial: the earliest known worked gold in the Americas.
notes: Source: https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.0710937105; F1.5 spec claim 12. links: INV081

name: Douroula
making_significance: Douroula has "the oldest evidence of the development of iron production found in Burkina Faso"; whether smelting south of the Sahara began there is argued.
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1602/; F1.5 spec claim 13; F1.6 spec claim 4. links: INV087

name: Umataka
date_note: Middle Jōmon, about 5,000 years ago; found 1936
making_significance: The flame pot found here in 1936 gave the flame-style type its name; it is an Important Cultural Property in the Nagaoka museum.
defined_by: Nagaoka Municipal Science Museum; Nakamura Kozaburo
notes: Source: https://api.sketchfab.com/v3/models/ce7aedf779a741239c664ba3d6c4448a; https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/R2-01251.html; F1.5 spec claim 10. links: INS101

name: Deir el-Bahri (Tomb MMA 101)
making_significance: The Met's excavation of a Theban tomb yielded a bronze mason's chisel (Met 27.3.12).
notes: Source: https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/544301; F1.6 spec claim 3. Content note: from a tomb. F1.5 names the place without a separate source.

name: Hōryūji
date_note: held Hyakumantō pagodas; gave 3,000 away in 1908
making_significance: The temple held many of the million pagodas and in 1908 gave 3,000 to contributors to a fund appeal.
notes: Source: Met 30.47a–c (https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/44955); F1.16 spec claim 6; F1.5 spec §5. links: OCC222

name: Rui'an
making_significance: Clan genealogies are printed here with wooden movable type, a practice UNESCO inscribed in 2010.
notes: Source: https://ich.unesco.org/en/USL/wooden-movable-type-printing-of-china-00322?USL=00322; F1.5 spec claim 25. links: PRA078

name: Dongyuan
making_significance: The village where Wang Chaohui prints genealogies with wooden movable type.
notes: Source: https://news.cgtn.com/news/3d3d514d77496a4e33457a6333566d54/index.html; F1.5 spec §10. links: PRA078

name: Faras Cemetery 1
making_significance: A Meroitic cemetery at Faras; grave 1007 held the cup now Met 13.125.37.
notes: Source: Met 13.125.37 (WS-016), F1.6 spec §2. Grave goods only, with a burial content note. links: PLC017

name: Huejotzingo
making_significance: Nahua leaders of Huejotzingo made a painted testimony in 1531 in a lawsuit over excessive tribute, including a feather and gold Madonna.
defined_by: the community's leaders; the Library of Congress
free_sources: Library of Congress ("free to use and reuse")
notes: Source: https://www.loc.gov/item/mss47662-2657/; https://smarthistory.org/codex-huexotzinco/; F1.7 spec claims 19–21. links: COM119; MKR020

name: Xiaomintun foundry
making_significance: A Shang foundry site with "bronze foundries, residences and burials"; the authors read the casters as "free from subsistence activities".
notes: Source: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0176329; F1.8 spec claim 5. Burials are not shown. links: PLC186

name: Raozhou
making_significance: Jingdezhen's prefecture: in 1433 an official brought court patterns there to fire 443,500 pieces.
notes: Source: Da Ming huidian juan 194 (http://ab.newdu.com/book/ms46965.html); F1.8 spec claim 13. links: PLC192

name: Manwoldae
making_significance: The Goryeo palace site at Kaeseong, where celadon roof tiles were found, supporting the record that King Uijong roofed a pavilion with them in 1157.
notes: Source: https://www.museum.go.kr/ENG/contents/E0403000000.do?schM=relic_represent_view&relicId=3129; F1.8 spec. links: PLC198

name: Taoxichuan
making_significance: A redeveloped factory district in Jingdezhen whose market picks 1,200 stallholders a month from over 4,000 (People's Daily, 2025).
notes: Source: https://en.people.cn/n3/2025/0719/c90000-20342418.html; F1.8 spec claim 22. Figures as state media gives them. links: PLC192; PRA069

name: Sripuranthan Brihadeeswarar temple
making_significance: A Tamil Nadu temple from which a Chola bronze Shiva Nataraja was stolen and later returned from Australia.
notes: Source: https://nga.gov.au/media/dd/documents/qa_update_shiva_nataraja.pdf; F1.9 spec claim 13. links: OBT201; OCC307

name: Qasr-i Abu Nasr
making_significance: The Met excavated an Achaemenid livestock tally here in 1935 and received it in a division of finds in 1936.
notes: Source: Met 36.30.62 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/323243); F1.9a spec claim 16. links: OCC310; INS108

name: Nashshān
date_note: documents early 1st millennium BCE to 6th century CE
making_significance: Most South Arabian palm-stalk documents come from this site, found by local people in the 1970s.
notes: Source: https://anetoday.org/stein-arabia-documents/; F1.9a spec claim 23. War in Yemen since 2015: link out only, no image (F1.9a spec §2).

name: Jebel Hafit
date_note: Hafit period c. 3200–2600 BCE; tombs ca. 2500 BCE
making_significance: Stone tombs of the Hafit period, part of the Cultural Sites of Al Ain (World Heritage, 2011).
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1343; F1.9a spec claims 6–7. links: ARC060

name: Hili
making_significance: Hili, in Al Ain, has "one of the oldest examples" of aflaj, from the Iron Age (UNESCO).
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1343; F1.9a spec claims 7, 24. Contested origin of aflaj (INV137; TEC220).

name: Sultan Hasan complex
making_significance: The Cairo complex of Sultan Hasan, endowed by waqf, hung with Mamluk glass lamps; a Swiss photochrom shows it for tourists.
free_sources: Library of Congress ("No known restrictions on publication")
notes: Source: LOC 2017657142 (https://www.loc.gov/item/2017657142/); F1.10 spec claim 13. links: PER308; OBT024

name: Staalhof
making_significance: The drapers' guild hall in Amsterdam, where "The Syndics" hung.
notes: Source: Rijksmuseum SK-C-6 (https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/SK-C-6); F1.11 spec claim 16. The hall is not named on the record as fetched (F1.11 spec).

name: Lugdunum red-gloss workshops
making_significance: Red-gloss workshops at Lyon produced stamped bowls, carried to frontier forts; stamps name people in production, including enslaved and freed workers.
notes: Source: Valkhof bowl (Europeana record, as for Utilis); Fülle 1997 (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-roman-studies/article/abs/internal-organization-of-the-arretine-terra-sigillata-industry-problems-of-evidence-and-interpretation/73AD21990173E86AA8F2C6968CC49845); F1.11 spec claims 6–7. links: TEC041; PER517

name: Kops Plateau
making_significance: A Roman military site at Nijmegen where a bowl stamped by Utilis of Lyon was found, its graffito naming a cavalry turma.
notes: Source: Europeana record as for Utilis; F1.11 spec claim 7. links: PER517; INS112

name: Wuatam (Watom) Island
making_significance: Lapita sherds dug on the island by a missionary in 1908–09 are now in Museums Victoria; the Rakival People speak for the island.
notes: Source: https://collections.museumsvictoria.com.au/api/items/187023; https://collections.museumsvictoria.com.au/api/articles/16808; F1.12 spec claim 12. links: ARC224; COM302

name: Rakival
making_significance: The Rakival village area of Wuatam (Watom) Island, whose people wrote in 2020 about what remains "unrevealed of our island".
notes: Source: https://collections.museumsvictoria.com.au/api/articles/16774; F1.12 spec claim 13. links: COM302

name: Yanghai cemetery
making_significance: Tombs near Turfan held wool trousers "shaped on the loom", called "a predecessor of modern riding" trousers.
notes: Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1040618214002808; F1.12a spec claim 8. links: INV104

name: Qamsar
making_significance: Near Kashan; "the most cited source" of the cobalt used for blue glazes; Abu'l-Qasim places lâjvard there.
notes: Source: https://www.mdpi.com/2075-163x/11/6/633; F1.13 spec claim 4. Contested against Anarak. links: TEC037; MAT128

name: Anarak
making_significance: Deposits about 200 km east of Kashan; Jiang et al. (2020) argue its ores "might have served as one of the most likely sources" of early Chinese cobalt.
notes: Source: https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1916630117; F1.13 spec claim 4. Contested against Qamsar. links: TEC037; MAT128

name: Futa Toro
making_significance: The Senegal River region where Omar ibn Said was born.
notes: Source: https://www.loc.gov/item/2018371864/; F1.13 spec claim 22.

name: Guran, Qeshm
making_significance: Shipwrights (jallaf) at Guran build lenj and spoke in 2017 of learning from their fathers and of orders drying up.
notes: Source: https://www.shaunbusuttil.com/stories/iran/the-last-shipbuilders-qeshm-island-lenj; F1.13 spec claim 24. Linked, not reproduced (AR-085). links: PRA143; TEC144

name: Shrine of St Thomas Becket, Canterbury
making_significance: Badges showing the shrine were sold to pilgrims at Canterbury; the shrine was destroyed in 1538.
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/473470; F1.16 spec claim 20. links: OBT340

name: Ikere palace
date_note: post c. 1910–14; in the palace until at least 1964
making_significance: The palace of the Ogoga of Ikere, an Ekiti Yorùbá kingdom, where Olowe of Ise's veranda post stood until at least 1964.
free_sources: Art Institute of Chicago (public domain); community-published site
notes: Source: https://api.artic.edu/api/v1/artworks/102611; https://ogogaikere.com/; F1.17 spec claim 13. Eshu figure: describe as the museum does. links: PER014

name: Guabba
making_significance: A Girsu account lists 4,272 women and 1,800 children from Guabba in the weaving sector.
notes: Source: https://www.harappa.com/content/guabba-meluhhan-village-mesopotamia; F1.18 spec claim 1. links: INS092

name: Xunmalin
making_significance: 3,000 Muslim households, mostly weavers, were settled here under Ögödei to weave cloth of gold.
notes: Source: https://archive.org/stream/WhenSilkWasGoldCentralAsianChineseTextile/When_Silk_Was_Gold_Central_Asian_and_Chinese_Textiles_djvu.txt; F1.19a spec claim 5. links: OBT345; OCC035

name: Hongzhou
making_significance: 300 Central Asian weavers and goldsmiths and 300 Chinese weavers were settled here to make cloth of gold.
notes: Source: https://archive.org/stream/WhenSilkWasGoldCentralAsianChineseTextile/When_Silk_Was_Gold_Central_Asian_and_Chinese_Textiles_djvu.txt; F1.19a spec claim 5. links: OBT345

name: Besh Baliq
making_significance: A third weaving community moved by the Mongols was settled at Besh Baliq.
notes: Source: https://archive.org/stream/WhenSilkWasGoldCentralAsianChineseTextile/When_Silk_Was_Gold_Central_Asian_and_Chinese_Textiles_djvu.txt; F1.19a spec claim 5. links: OBT345

name: Hwéeldi (Bosque Redondo)
making_significance: More than 8,000 Diné were marched to Fort Sumner and held at Bosque Redondo; Cleveland links the turn to rugs for collectors to the trade networks broken there.
notes: Source: https://npshistory.com/publications/hutr/brochures/churro-sheep.pdf; https://clevelandart.org/art/1937.903; F1.19a spec claim 18. The place of OCC141. links: OCC141

name: Durbar Room, Osborne
making_significance: Queen Victoria's room at Osborne, "designed by … Lockwood Kipling, and master carver Bhai Ram Singh" (English Heritage).
leaves_out: the craftsmen who cast the moulds
notes: Source: https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/places/osborne/things-to-do/state-rooms; F1.19b spec claim 10. links: PER554; PER241

name: Tashkent
making_significance: The Uzbek capital, rebuilt after the 1966 earthquake with modernist buildings that adapted "standardised systems to regional materials, traditions".
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1766/; F1.20 spec claims 6, 9. links: PLC467; OCC323

name: Tashkent Modernist Architecture
other_names: Tashkent Modernist Architecture. Modernity and Tradition in Central Asia
date_note: buildings of the 1960s to early 1990s; inscribed 2026
making_significance: A World Heritage group of ten Tashkent buildings inscribed for adapting "standardised systems to regional materials, traditions, and environment".
leaves_out: the brigades of craftsmen and the earlier city
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1766/; F1.20 spec claim 9 and §10.

name: Peoples' Friendship Palace, Tashkent
making_significance: Its façade is "panjara screens reimagined in concrete and stone" (Yevgeny Rozanov, Elena Sukhanova).
notes: Source: https://www.archdaily.com/1038318/soviet-architecture-of-tashkent-ten-key-buildings-of-hybrid-modernism; F1.20 spec claim 10. links: PLC467

name: Navoi Theatre, Tashkent
making_significance: Alexey Shchusev's theatre was carved in ganch by masters including Usto Shirin Muradov; Soviet Koreans worked on it from 1943 and Japanese prisoners of war "assisted".
notes: Source: https://kun.uz/en/20430948; http://ich.uz/en/ich-of-uzbekistan/national-list/domain-5/441-ganchkorlik; F1.20 spec claims 6–7. Opening year and prisoners' numbers unverified. links: PER563; COM304

name: Almaty
making_significance: In Almaty "dozens of works of monumental art were produced at the Oner Art Combine by brigades of craftsmen".
notes: Source: https://www.new-east-archive.org/features/show/11093/almaty-monumental-art-dennis-keen; F1.20 spec claim 12. links: MKR101

name: Chandigarh
making_significance: The new Punjab capital; UNESCO (2016) says its Capitol Complex "symbolized India's accession to modernity".
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1321/; F1.20 spec claims 3, 15. links: STY056; PER255

name: Brasília
making_significance: Brazil's capital was built to plans by Lúcio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer under Kubitschek.
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/445/; F1.20 spec claim 17. links: PER566

name: Taobao village
making_significance: A village with at least 100 active online shops and 10 million yuan of yearly sales, such as the furniture sellers of Dongfeng, Jiangsu.
notes: Source: https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2019/11/22/stimulating-jobs-growth-entrepreneurship-income-in-rural-china-through-e-commerce; F1.21 spec claim 18. A place type.

name: Chincha Islands
making_significance: Peru's guano came mainly from these islands, dug by enslaved people, convicts, Indigenous workers and Chinese contract workers.
notes: Source: https://heritage.lrfoundation.org.uk/stories/guano-the-perilous-cargo-of-flammable-and-noxious-fertiliser; NYPL photograph (https://digitalcollections.nypl.org/items/ab4769e0-c61a-012f-0974-58d385a7bc34); F1.22 spec claim 7. links: MAT126; NET061

name: Humberstone and Santa Laura Saltpeter Works
making_significance: The works processed "the largest deposit of saltpeter in the world"; pampinos from Chile, Peru and Bolivia made nitrate fertiliser.
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1178/; F1.22 spec claim 9. links: NET061

name: Aral Sea
making_significance: The Soviet Union diverted the Aral Sea's two rivers for cotton; by 2014 the sea covered about 10% of its 1960 area.
notes: Source: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/world-of-change/aral-sea/; F1.22 spec claims 15–16. links: OCC231

name: Shakhrisabz
making_significance: Cleveland's suzani, silk embroidery on six strips of cotton cloth, was "probably embroidered in Shakhrisyabz" for a dowry.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 2016.89 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/2016.89); F1.22 spec §10. links: STY165

name: Bayan Obo
making_significance: In 2012 NASA said about half of China's rare-earth output came from this mine, with acid waste gas, wastewater and radioactive residue.
notes: Source: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/rare-earth-in-bayan-obo-77723/; F1.22 spec claim 18. The share is dated 2012. links: MAT137

name: Hyde Park Barracks, Sydney
making_significance: Barracks designed by Francis Greenway and built by convicts; one of the Australian Convict Sites.
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1306/; F1.23 spec claim 15. Membership of the UNESCO group is from an encyclopaedia. links: PLC480

name: Australian Convict Sites
making_significance: Eleven sites record the transportation of about 166,000 people to Australia, with "forced labour to help build the colony".
notes: Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1306/; F1.23 spec claim 15 and §10.

name: Stony Bluff Manufactory
making_significance: A stoneware pottery in Old Edgefield District, South Carolina, where the enslaved potter and poet Dave signed a storage jar with a couplet in 1858.
leaves_out: the potters who did not sign
notes: Source: Met 2020.7 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/747045); F1.23 spec claim 1. links: OBT359

name: Kamay
making_significance: Where four spears were taken on 29 April 1770 and sent to Trinity College; they were returned in 2024.
notes: Source: https://www.trin.cam.ac.uk/news/return-of-the-gweagal-spears-to-the-la-perouse-aboriginal-community/; F1.24 spec claim 17. links: COM305

name: Tauric Chersonesos
making_significance: One of four Crimean museums whose objects were on loan in Amsterdam in 2014.
notes: Source: https://allardpierson.nl/nieuws/alle-objecten-uit-de-krim-terug-in-oekraine/; F1.24 spec claim 8.

name: Xigoupan tomb 2
making_significance: Gold belt plaques from tomb 2 are tied to "the pre-imperial period Qin workshop".
notes: Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s40494-021-00520-5; F1.25 spec claim 7. The shaofu inscription is not in the passages read (F1.25 spec §10). links: ARC231

name: Fangmatan
making_significance: A fragment found on a body in a Western Han tomb may be paper, roughly 250–280 years before Cai Lun, and may be a map.
notes: Source: https://press.uchicago.edu/books/HOC/HOC_V2_B2/HOC_VOLUME2_Book2_chapter3.pdf; F1.27 spec claim 2. Whether it is paper is contested. links: INV036; PER161

name: Panjakent
making_significance: Sogdian city whose lord Devastich left 76 writings in Sogdian, Arabic and Chinese on leather, wood and paper before the Arabs took him in 722.
notes: Source: https://edspace.american.edu/silkroadjournal/wp-content/uploads/sites/984/2017/09/Silk-Road-or-Paper-Road.pdf; F1.27 spec claim 4. links: POL228; TEC185

name: Suq al-warraqin
making_significance: Baghdad's market had "more than one hundred shops for paper- and booksellers".
notes: Source: Bloom (https://edspace.american.edu/silkroadjournal/wp-content/uploads/sites/984/2017/09/Silk-Road-or-Paper-Road.pdf); F1.27 spec claim 6. One source.

name: Xàtiva
making_significance: Arab paper mills worked here around 1050.
notes: Source: https://www.handpapermaking.org/magazine-articles/italy-the-birthplace-of-western-paper-tracing-the-development-and-spread-of-fabriano-paper; F1.27 spec claim 9. links: TEC186

name: Fabriano
making_significance: An Italian papermaking town credited with hammer beaters, gelatin sizing and watermarks, often titled "the birthplace of Western paper".
notes: Source: https://www.handpapermaking.org/magazine-articles/italy-the-birthplace-of-western-paper-tracing-the-development-and-spread-of-fabriano-paper; F1.27 spec claim 9. The "birthplace" title is read as framing. links: TEC186

name: Erdene Zuu
making_significance: The monastery at Karakorum; the Mongol palace "has to be looked for underneath" it.
notes: Source: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s41826-020-00039-x; F1.28 spec claim 6. links: PLC258

name: Great Hall of Karakorum
making_significance: Read since 1933 as Ögedei's palace, the hall was almost completely uncovered 2001–05 and is now identified as a large Buddhist temple.
notes: Source: https://orchontal.de/en/monuments/karakorum/great-hall/; F1.28 spec claim 5. links: PLC258

name: Khotan
making_significance: Xuanzang wrote that Khotan once "knew nothing about mulberry trees or silkworms" until a princess brought them.
notes: Source: https://archive.org/details/siyukibuddhistre02hsuoft; F1.29 spec claim 8. links: OCC342; NET003

name: Dandan-Uiliq
making_significance: A shrine site from which Stein removed a votive panel painting the silk princess, now in the British Museum.
notes: Source: https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/A_1907-1111-73; F1.29 spec claim 9. links: OCC342

name: El Perú-Waka'
making_significance: A Maya site whose stela of Lady K'abel (692) was cut up and reached Cleveland in 1967; how it left Guatemala is not recorded.
notes: Source: https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1967.29; https://traffickingculture.org/encyclopedia/case-studies/el-peru-waka-stela-fragment-returned-to-guatemala-in-1999/; F1.30 spec claim 15. Link-out only (AR-043).

name: Tikal
making_significance: A sapodilla-wood lintel at Tikal with a Long Count date was radiocarbon-dated to 658–696.
notes: Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/srep01597; F1.30 spec claim 14. The polity is POL046. links: POL046

name: Ottoman Empire
date_note: conventional dates; the endonym is to verify (F1.1 spec)
making_significance: The Ottoman court ran design studios and workshops, endowed mosques and libraries through waqf, and drew İznik ceramics and court textiles into one visual programme.
leaves_out: the many peoples, languages and faiths it ruled; enslaved people in the palace (Beshir Agha was enslaved as a boy); provincial workshops
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0); Library of Congress (public-domain items)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1995.17 and 1944.236 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1995.17); Hathaway, Beshir Agha (2005), publisher page https://nes.princeton.edu/publications/beshir-agha-chief-eunuch-ottoman-imperial-harem; F1.10 spec claims 10, 15. No Ottoman polity or dynasty row existed (F1.1, F1.10 specs). links: PRD169; STY109; INS042; OCC055

name: Nōgaku
making_significance: The theatre of Noh and kyōgen keeps masks, costumes and carving lineages in use.
notes: Source: F1.4 spec §10 names it for UNESCO (unverified 3 Oct 2026); no page opened. Under review: UNESCO status not checked.

name: Falaj water-share keeping, Oman
date_note: UNESCO World Heritage 2006 (Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman)
making_significance: Communities share falaj water by time: a day of 48 athar, run by a wakil with a banker (qabidh or amin al-daftar).
leaves_out: UAE aflaj, left to F1.31's local authors
notes: Source: Al-Ghafri 2021 (https://ishraqa.unizwa.edu.om/article_169721.html); Oman Water Society (https://www.omanws.org.om/Water%20body%20pages/Water%20sources/water_sources/aflaj.html); F1.9a spec claim 25 and §2. The falaj step is held for an Omani reader (F1.9a spec §9). links: INV137; TEC220

name: Ijaza
making_significance: Calligraphers pass on the craft through ijaza, a teacher's licence that ties a student into a lineage of masters.
notes: Source: UNESCO 2021, Arabic calligraphy element (states' file), cited in F1.10 spec §2; https://www.scriptsnscribes.com/blogs/2021/8/13/a-conversation-with-master-calligrapher-yushaa-abdullah. links: PRA130

name: Mongol nomad migration
other_names: Mongol nomad migration and its associated practices
making_significance: Herders move with their animals across the seasons; children learn "assembling and disassembling yurts".
notes: Source: https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/mongol-nomad-migration-and-its-associated-practices-02091; F1.22a spec claim 6. Proposed by F1.12a and F1.22a. links: OBT001; COM213

name: Jebena buna (Ethiopian coffee ceremony)
making_significance: Coffee is brewed in a clay jebena, "usually crafted by an elderly woman", and served in three rounds, the third called baraka, "to be blessed".
notes: Source: https://www.maadigitallab.org/blog/2023/08/22/at-the-heart-of-the-jebena-bunna-the-ethiopian-coffee-ceremony/; F1.16 spec claim 19. links: OBT087

name: Uli
making_significance: An Igbo women's painting practice that Uche Okeke, who learned it from his mother, drew on for Zaria's Natural Synthesis.
leaves_out: the women who held the practice
notes: Source: https://smarthistory.org/uche-okeke/; F1.20 spec claim 20. links: MOV072

name: Mongolian traditional feltmaking custom
making_significance: Mongolian families make felt together in late summer or early autumn, shaping new felt on an old "mother felt".
defined_by: National Center for Cultural Heritage, Mongolia
notes: Source: https://ncch.gov.mn/ich?ItemID=14; F1.22a spec claim 7. UNESCO status not given in the spec. links: TEC100; TEC238

name: Kolhapuri chappal making
making_significance: Leather artisans make the Kolhapuri sandal, whose geographical indication (2019) is held by two state corporations.
notes: Source: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/7/1/why-is-prada-caught-in-a-sandal-scandal-in-india; https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/story/india%2Fmaharashtra%2Fprada-kolhapuri-chappal-row-two-govt-agencies-officially-hold-gi-tag-for-sandals-3661799; F1.26 spec claim 17. Caste named only as a source states it (F1.26 spec §2). links: INS143; INS144

name: Ka Mate
making_significance: A haka composed by Te Rauparaha; commercial uses must credit him and Ngāti Toa Rangatira.
notes: Source: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2014/0018/latest/whole.html; F1.26 spec claim 11. links: OCC336

name: Art of Akyns, Kyrgyz epic tellers
making_significance: Kyrgyz epic tellers whose art "combines singing, improvisation and musical composition".
notes: Source: https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/00065; F1.29 spec claim 6. links: COM209

name: Kyrgyz epic trilogy: Manas, Semetey, Seytek
making_significance: The Manas trilogy is told for "up to thirteen hours" by "women and men, of all ages", passed from master to apprentice.
notes: Source: https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/kyrgyz-epic-trilogy-manas-semetey-seytek-00876; F1.29 spec claim 6. links: COM209

name: Jemdet Nasr period
date_note: c. 3100–2900 BCE (the Met's date for the tablet)
making_significance: The Met dates its proto-cuneiform barley account to the Jemdet Nasr period; tablets of this phase record grain, rations and labour.
free_sources: Met Open Access (public domain records); PeriodO (link-out)
notes: Source: Met 1988.433.1 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/329081), F1.1 spec claim 1. links: PRD031; ARC054; INV001

name: Hijri era
making_significance: The Islamic lunar era, counted from the Hijra; makers dated objects in it, as on a 690 AH astrolabe.
notes: Source: https://www.fourmilab.ch/documents/calendar/; Met 444408; F1.30 spec claims 1, 3.

name: Jalali / Solar Hijri calendar
making_significance: A solar calendar whose year begins at the March equinox, adopted under Malik-Shah I with astronomers including Omar Khayyam.
notes: Source: https://www.fourmilab.ch/documents/calendar/; https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/calendars-iii-afghan-calendars; F1.30 spec claim 5.

name: Sexagenary cycle
date_note: days on Shang oracle bones; years from about the mid-3rd century BCE
making_significance: A cycle pairing ten stems with twelve branches, used to date days and years and found in inscriptions on made things.
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexagenary_cycle; F1.30 spec claim 7.

name: Japanese era names (nengō)
date_note: Act on Era Names (Act No. 43 of 1979)
making_significance: Japan names years by reign era and still does so in law.
notes: Source: https://www.japaneselawtranslation.go.jp/en/laws/view/4844/en; F1.30 spec §10. links: PRD107

name: Twelve-animal cycle
date_note: Orkhon inscription year of the Sheep (731 CE)
making_significance: Years named after twelve animals, used in Old Turkic inscriptions and explained in al-Kashgari's Dīwān (1072–74).
notes: Source: https://cyberleninka.ru/article/n/life-and-time-in-orkhon-yenisey-monuments/pdf; F1.30 spec claim 9.

name: Long Count and Calendar Round
date_note: earliest known dates 36 BCE (Chiapa de Corzo) and 32 BCE (Tres Zapotes)
making_significance: Mesoamerican day counts carved on stelae and lintels; a k'atun is 7,200 days, and a Tikal lintel's date supports the GMT correlation.
notes: Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/srep01597; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesoamerican_Long_Count_calendar; F1.30 spec claims 13–14. Correlation probable. links: PRD180; INV009

name: Ethiopian calendar
making_significance: A calendar whose year number runs seven or eight behind the Gregorian, with a thirteenth month; New Year is 11 September.
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_calendar; F1.30 spec claim 11. links: PRD024

name: Indian national calendar (Śaka era)
making_significance: India's national calendar, counted in the Śaka era, adopted after a reform committee headed by Meghnad Saha.
notes: Source: https://www.fourmilab.ch/documents/calendar/; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_national_calendar; F1.30 spec claim 10. Year 0 at 78 CE or the 79 equinox, by convention. links: PER608

name: Hebrew calendar
making_significance: A lunisolar calendar with a leap month in 7 of every 19 years; tradition credits Hillel II with fixing it.
notes: Source: https://www.fourmilab.ch/documents/calendar/; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_calendar; F1.30 spec claim 12. Hillel date contested.

name: Seleucid era
date_note: Hillel II's year 670 of the era = 358–359 CE
making_significance: An era used in the Hebrew calendar's tradition: Hillel II is said to have fixed the calendar "in the year 670 of the Seleucid era".
notes: Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_calendar; F1.30 spec claim 12. links: PRD051

name: Descriptive specialty
making_significance: Vaudeville recording artists made sound scenes of trades such as "In a country blacksmith shop"; many used ethnic and racial caricature.
notes: Source: https://adp.library.ucsb.edu/index.php/objects/detail/33030/Victor_4106; F1.4 spec claim 5 and §2. Discs must be heard in full before use (F1.4 spec §9).

name: European "Mamluk" revival glass
making_significance: European glassmakers copied enamelled Mamluk lamps and bottles; records and lab tests, not the eye, tell a revival piece from a medieval one.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1981.10 and 1944.488 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1981.10); F1.10 spec claim 20. links: TEC049; STY104

name: "Zandaniji"
making_significance: A label for silks once read as Sogdian work from Zandana near Bukhara; Sims-Williams and Khan (2008) re-read the inscription as Arabic.
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: Cleveland 1974.190 (https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1974.190); https://invisibleeast.site.ox.ac.uk/article/invisible-and-visible-sogdians-and-their-silks; F1.19 spec claim 15. Contested label (spec: "as a GAP row"); filed as a style. links: CIV088

name: Linear Elamite
date_note: late 3rd millennium BCE (standard range; not given in the spec)
making_significance: A script of ancient Iran; Desset and colleagues claimed its decipherment in 2022, which Dahl (2023) questioned.
leaves_out: the provenance of the Mahboubian vessels used
notes: Source: https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-paper/v47/n04/tom-stevenson/beyond-mesopotamia; F1.9a spec claim 14. Contested decipherment.

name: Proto-Elamite script
making_significance: Proto-Elamite tablets record state transactions and remain undeciphered.
notes: Source: https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-paper/v47/n04/tom-stevenson/beyond-mesopotamia; F1.9a spec claims 14–15. links: ARC056

name: South Arabian minuscule on palm stalks
date_note: early 1st millennium BCE to 6th century CE
making_significance: Scribes cut letters, accounts and contracts into palm stalks in a cursive South Arabian script.
notes: Source: https://anetoday.org/stein-arabia-documents/; F1.9a spec claim 23.

name: Roman cast-and-point copying
making_significance: Roman workshops took moulds and plaster casts of Greek originals and copied them in marble or bronze; copies were valued, not seen as lesser.
notes: Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/roman-copies-of-greek-statues; F1.14 spec claim 6. links: GAP067

name: Kōwhaiwhai
making_significance: Painted scroll patterns in the wharenui; in Deidre Brown's words the ancestors' "descendants are depicted in kōwhaiwhai painted sequences and poupou".
notes: Source: https://teara.govt.nz/en/maori-architecture-whare-maori/print; F1.15 spec §2. Link-out only: no specific kōwhaiwhai shown (F1.15 spec). links: COM288; PER356

name: Ganchkorlik (ganch carving)
making_significance: Carving in gypsum plaster (ganch), listed on Uzbekistan's national heritage list; masters decorated the Navoi Theatre.
notes: Source: http://ich.uz/en/ich-of-uzbekistan/national-list/domain-5/441-ganchkorlik; F1.20 spec claim 7.

name: Metal-staple ceramic repair
making_significance: In China broken ceramics "were typically mended with metal staples", where Japan used gold lacquer.
notes: Source: Met 48373 (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/48373); F1.22a spec claim 2. links: TEC223

name: Ekh esgii (mother felt)
making_significance: New Mongolian felt is shaped on an old sheet, the ekh esgii ("mother felt"), made by families together in late summer.
defined_by: National Center for Cultural Heritage, Mongolia
notes: Source: https://ncch.gov.mn/ich?ItemID=14; F1.22a spec claim 7. Single source. links: TEC100

name: Life-casting
making_significance: Casting moulds from living animals and plants; Smith and Beentjes argue it was "viewed in part as a means to the knowledge of nature".
notes: Source: https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/652535; F1.28a spec claim 6. links: TEC058; PER396

name: Apocryphal reign mark
making_significance: Potters wrote an earlier reign's mark on later wares, as Kangxi pieces carry "Da Ming Chenghua nian zhi"; Cleveland calls the mark "apocryphal".
leaves_out: the potters and painters of both reigns
free_sources: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0)
notes: Source: https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1957.61; https://openaccess-api.clevelandart.org/api/artworks/1964.218; F1.30 spec claim 8. Why they used the older mark is interpretive. links: PRD107; PRD102
